findings.location: V2.4 section 0 line 32 and D-1 line 55 (citation 'BA-11, section 1'); BA-11 V3 section 2.1 seal order (line 55) and BA-01 row DEPENDS_ON 'none' (line 61)
findings.claim: The contract identity rule cites a byte procedure in a draft, versioned artifact that is sealed last. Nothing links a later change of that procedure back to BA-01, so a later BA-11 version could change how the contract composite is computed without expiring BA-01's candidate or seal.
findings.evidence: V2.4 cites 'the hash registry (baseline artifact BA-11, section 1)' with no version or blob, as AR2-02 prescribes. BA-11 is DRAFT V3; its seal order is 'BA-01 -> ... -> BA-11 (last)'; BA-01 DEPENDS_ON = none; and the cascade rule expires only dependents of a changed entry. V2.4 cannot pin a BA-11 blob, because BA-11 V3 section 4 already contains V2.4's blob id, and pinning in the other direction would create a cycle.
findings.required_fix: Do not change V2.4. Either BA-11 declares that its section 1 'contract composite hash' row is part of BA-01's identity, so any change to it is a new contract composite and expires the BA-01 candidate or seal and its dependents; or the Coordinator's textual-verification record pins the BA-11 blob and section whose procedure V2.4 cites.

rulings.item: Is V2.4 revision 2 ready for the Coordinator's textual verification?
rulings.recommendation: YES: READY_FOR_COORDINATOR_TEXTUAL_VERIFICATION. The six MINOR findings (V24R2-01..06) should be recorded in, or closed by, that verification. None of them blocks it.
rulings.reasoning: (1) Section 1 is byte-identical to the reviewed draft: the 768-byte span from '## 1.' to '## 2.' matches between blob 1919a32a (d190ec09) and blob fc137c52 (1625a306). The line starting '> The baseline requires' (696 characters) is also identical to line 116 of the recorded phase-1 ruling, backticks included. (2) The full diff of d190ec09..1625a306 on this file touches only the header, section 0, the section 2 rows, section 3 and section 4. Each change traces to AR2-01..AR2-07 or is a pointer or metadata line. The AR2-02, AR2-03, AR2-05 and AR2-06 texts are faithful renderings. (3) The blobs of V1, V2, V2.1, V2.2 and V2.3 (135c26e0, 9254b1a2, 6259a3be, fd7260c5, bc3d67a9) are unchanged. (4) The composite in BA-11 V3 section 4 reproduces exactly over the revision-2 blob. (5) All 8 prior findings (V24-01..07, XC-F10) are FIXED. No state changes and no new state is introduced. The new findings are one factual miscount in implementer text, two unresolved anchors inside the Architect's own pre-approved wording, one provenance overclaim, and two BA-11-side identity-wiring points. None of them alters the effect of V2.4.

rulings.item: How to apply byte corrections to V2.4 without breaking identity
rulings.recommendation: If the Coordinator wants V24R2-01 and/or V24R2-04 fixed in the bytes, issue a revision 3 limited to lines 26 and 61, with section 1 untouched. The header then cites revision 2 (blob fc137c52, commit 1625a306) as reviewed. BA-11 V3 section 4 (blob id and CANDIDATE_COMPOSITE_HASH) is regenerated in the same commit. Otherwise, record both as readings in the textual-verification record and keep blob fc137c52.
rulings.reasoning: Any byte change to V2.4 changes its blob id, and with it the composite recorded in BA-11. Leaving the two out of step would recreate the identity drift that the phase-2 review measured (74725e4d versus b308d8ce).

rulings.item: Precedence of the NB-4 row over V2.3
rulings.recommendation: No text change. The Coordinator records that V2.4 prevails over V2.3 for the NB-4 row by the 'Effective contract' row (V2.2, V2.3 and V2.4 applied in that order).
rulings.reasoning: The AR2-03 precedence text names V2.1 and V2.2 for section 2 clauses. The AR2-05 NB-4 row also reads V2.3's blocker table (V2.3 line 147). The row is a reading that changes no state, so no conflict arises, and the application order already settles precedence. Changing the pre-approved AR2-03 wording would need a new Architect pre-approval, which is not warranted.

rulings.item: Anchors inside pre-approved wording (V24R2-02 'item (10)', V24R2-03 'LEARNING entry of the EVM')
rulings.recommendation: The Architect fixes both anchors in the delta ruling: item (10) = phase-1 section 7 BA-06/NB-4 step 2, equivalently section 10 B.1; the LEARNING-side citation lives in BA-06 (EVM-level field or EVM_FROZEN pin record). The implementer must not reword V24-N2.
rulings.reasoning: AR2-06 pre-approved these words verbatim, and the implementer applied them exactly. Only the author of the text can say which anchors were meant. The Coordinator's textual verification needs resolvable anchors, because section 0 now names the recorded phase-1 file as the source.

findings.location: BA-02b section 1 rule 1 (line 18); section 4 rows Q (line 100), SC-B (116), PR-REC (118) and PW-CLONE (121). JSON: PW-CLONE-WRONG-TYPE (line 6095), PR-CLOSURE-COMPLETENESS (6414), WR-A-X7 (9869), WR-B-X0 (12765) and the other X7/X8 cells.
findings.claim: Rule 1 says BA-04 V3 derives GROUPS_SERVED with the AR2-08 rule, 'so sections 2 and 3 agree by construction'. That is false for 13 scenarios. As a result, three CONTROL groups (SC-B class B; PR-REC and PW-CLONE class A) receive PASS contributions and countable coverage from scenarios that exercise none of their controls, which AR2-08 forbids. BA02-F05 therefore persists in a narrower form.
findings.evidence:
I recomputed, for each of the 370 scenarios: GROUPS_SERVED minus the union of AFFECTED_GROUPS over CONTROLS_EXERCISED minus EVIDENCE_GROUPS_DECLARED. No scenario is missing a group, but 13 have extra CONTROL groups:
- WR-A-X7, WR-D-X7, WR-E-X7, WR-A-X8, WR-D-X8, WR-E-X8, WR-F-X8, WR-G-X8, WR-B-X0, WR-B-X7, WR-C-X7 serve SC-B. Their CONTROLS_EXERCISED is only S2, S3 (groups SC-A, KS) and their EVIDENCE_GROUPS_DECLARED is empty. Their EXPECTED_GROUP_VERDICT is 'PASS if the observed outcome and channel equal the declared expectation (contributes to the groups served)'.
- PW-CLONE-WRONG-TYPE serves PW-CLONE, but CLONE is not in its CONTROLS_EXERCISED.
- PR-CLOSURE-COMPLETENESS has CONTROLS_EXERCISED = [] and serves PR-REC with verdict 'PASS (EVIDENCE_COMPLETE)'. V2.2 PA-3 defines EVIDENCE_COMPLETE only for EVIDENCE-kind groups, and PR-REC is a CONTROL group (PA-1.3).

AR2-08: 'La cobertura de PASS cuenta solo los controles de CONTROLS_EXERCISED'. Section 4 still counts these scenarios as serving and 'governing and countable':
- SC-B: 112 serving / 106 countable
- PR-REC: 50 / 44
- PW-CLONE: 10 / 10
- Q: 26 / 1 (the 1 is PR-CLOSURE-COMPLETENESS)

The contract does assign some of these memberships: V2.1 10.8 line 587 ('group SC-B includes an X7 scenario per writer'); V2.2 PA-12 (CLOSURE_COMPLETENESS_CONTROL to group PR-REC; the variants of CLONE_NON_REPLACE_CONTROL to PW-CLONE). The closed AR2-08 rule admits only groups derived from controls plus declared evidence or NOT_A_CONTROL groups, and neither artifact records this exception.
findings.required_fix:
Either:
(a) obtain an Architect ruling that extends AR2-08 with a declared, contract-assigned membership (V2.1 10.8; V2.2 PA-12) that contributes evidence, never PASS; or
(b) make the 13 scenarios conform:
- add CLONE to the CONTROLS_EXERCISED of PW-CLONE-WRONG-TYPE (it is a PA-12 variant);
- declare the SC-B membership of the X7 cells through the NOT_A_CONTROL item POST_V1_TO_CP_QUEUE_LOG in EVIDENCE_GROUPS_DECLARED, with an evidence-only verdict, and handle the X8 and X0-ABA residual cells the same way;
- put PR-CLOSURE-COMPLETENESS in Q, or apply the ruled PR-REC membership, and replace 'EVIDENCE_COMPLETE' with a verdict valid for its group.
Then recompute section 4. Keep the 'agree by construction' sentence (and BA-04 md line 33) only if a committed mechanical check backs it.

findings.location: Section 2 row CLONE (line 57); line 59 ('Rows whose state is not COVERED_DRAFT: 0'); section 5 check 2 (line 138, 'PASS (in draft)')
findings.claim: CLONE_POLICY_VERIFIED (class A, IN_PREDICATE = YES) has no negative control and no recorded reason that it cannot be violated by design. The reason given, 'DESIGNED_STIMULUS', is a category that neither the phase-1 BASELINE_READY rule nor V2.1 31 check 2 provides. The row is still reported COVERED_DRAFT and check 2 is reported as PASS. This is the same defect pattern as BA02-F02 (E-03), introduced here by V3.
findings.evidence:
- BA-02b line 57: NEGATIVE CONTROLS '(none)'. Reason: 'DESIGNED_STIMULUS: the PA-12 variants present homonyms under the non-replacing policy; acceptance is success or REJECT, so the control is exercised by its variants, not violated'. STATE COVERED_DRAFT.
- Phase-1 ruling B (evidence file line 42): 'más uno de violación deliberada o el motivo registrado de que no puede violarse por diseño'. V2.1 31 check 2: 'unless the control cannot be violated by design (recorded with the reason)'. BA-02b's own rule 5 (line 22) repeats this. DESIGNED_STIMULUS does not claim the control cannot be violated.
- The registry (BA-02a line 72) maps a CLONE failure to 'FAIL / UNKNOWN; class-A row', so a violable condition exists. Examples: a declared cloning mode off the allow-list (V2.2 PA-12 keeps the V2.1 procedure), or an unreadable pre-existing fingerprint (compare PR-REC-UNREADABLE for S5REC). AR2-20 already accepts a fault switch in U-4.

findings.location: section 3, row 'authority of V17 3.7 / 3.8' (line 73), RESULT = IDENTICAL; compare rows 74-77 (NO_STATEMENT)
findings.claim: Row 73 is a meta row about the authority status of V17 sections, and it is classified IDENTICAL. The closed domain reserves IDENTICAL for 'same statement' and counts it as agreement. The authorities cited in row 73 make no statement about the Selective scope. The analogous meta rows 74-77 are NO_STATEMENT, and so is the contract's own analogue.
findings.evidence: V2.1 25.3 (line 1300) defines IDENTICAL as '(same statement)' and NO_STATEMENT as 'an authority that does not address the row; it is not a conflict and is not counted as agreement'. Foundation section 3 (blob 89a21b6f, line 59) classifies V17 sections 3.7/3.8 as `HISTORICAL ONLY`, a statement about the status of V17 sections. Post-I-57 section 2 item 2 (lines 33-34) limits a substitution. Neither states SEL-FRONTAL or SEL-PLANTA. The contract's counterpart row 'A_k provisional flag' (V2.1 line 1322) records 'resolved ... no material change found'. The contract row 'ownership of exposure' (line 1323) is NO_STATEMENT, as are BA-03 V3 rows 74-77. Condition 5 is unaffected.
findings.required_fix: Classify row 73 as NO_STATEMENT and keep the resolution (neutral plans only; exposure stays with I-52 per Foundation section 4, post-I-57 sections 2 and 4, and Freeze V18 section 7) in the NOTE, as rows 74-77 do. Alternatively, state an explicit rule for authority-status rows and have the Architect confirm it.

findings.location: section 3 row 'ownership of the exposure' NOTE (line 74); section 4 closing paragraph (line 103); checks P57_ZERO_* (json lines 279-354)
findings.claim: Row 74 gives 'zero occurrences of the PW-3 keywords' as the reason for NO_STATEMENT. But the PW-3 list is Spanish and code terms, and P57 states its exposure policy in English. The zero counts are literally true but cannot detect an exposure statement written the way P57 writes one.
findings.evidence: P57 blob 5f4933a3: line 71 reads '- mirror read-set, exposure policy y combinaciones view/kind admitidas;' (section 4); line 133 reads '- la matriz kind/view soportada;' (section 7); 'View' appears on lines 22, 35, 44 and 128. The zero-count patterns (frontal, planta, lateral, \bSection\b, exposici[oó]n, A_k, Selectiv) all return 0. V2.2 PW-3 (line 414) says the keyword search 'is not a complete review and is not sufficient for sealing'. The section-by-section reading (section 4 table) is correct and is the real basis for the conclusion.
findings.required_fix: Rest the NO_STATEMENT on the section-by-section reading and cite section 4's table in the NOTE. State that P57's exposure vocabulary is English ('exposure policy' at line 71, 'kind/view' at line 133), in the sections the reading classifies. Optionally add counted checks such as 'exposure' expected 1 and case-insensitive 'kind/view|view/kind' expected 2, so the reading can be reproduced.

findings.location: JSON scenarios E4-LEARN-R1-LM1, E4-LEARN-R1-LM2, LK-LM1-PROPS, LK-LM1-CONFLICT, LK-LM2-PROPS, LK-LM2-CONFLICT (fields EXPECTED_PRODUCT_OUTCOME, EXPECTED_EVENTS, EVM_VERSION, PIN_SLOTS, BLOCKED_BY, STATUS, MODE); md section 2 (K-3 limited to governing scenarios), section 2.1 (LOCK_MODE row), section 5.1 rows 244-249
findings.claim: The six non-governing runs that AR2-11 uses to derive the LOCK_MODE and E04_ADMITTED_SET@R-1 pins cannot reach PC. They expect a committed O3 and phase-A events 'of the pinned frozen EVM', but by AR2-11's own order no EVM exists when they run, and E-12 phase A stays fail-closed. The pins for PC and V1 therefore have no feasible source, and those pins gate 156 and 163 scenarios.
findings.evidence: E4-LEARN-R1-LM1 (the other five are the same): REACH CP; PLAN 'observation of D-1..D-6 at P0, PL, PV, PC'; EXPECTED_PRODUCT_OUTCOME 'O3 SUCCESS'; EXPECTED_EVENTS MUTATION (A) 'exactly the EXPECTED_MUTATION_EVENT_SET of the pinned frozen EVM for f(plan)'; EVM_VERSION 'NONE'; PIN_SLOTS ['FIXTURE_INSTANCE@FX-1F']; BLOCKED_BY []; STATUS SEALED_PENDING_PIN_CANDIDATE. CONTROLS_EXERCISED includes E12A, E12C, S1, S2 and S3, and EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS exempts only E03 and E04. AR2-11 fixes the order 'E4-LEARN-R1 ... -> LK-* -> selection of LOCK_MODE -> E-04 pin ... -> EVM learning -> validation', and only E-03 and E-04 are RECORDED_NOT_ENFORCED. V2.1 3.2 keeps E-01..E-13 fail-closed in every CHARACTERIZATION_RUN. V2.1 8 says 'an event not deterministically attributable aborts before Commit()', and with no model no event can be attributed, so the run aborts at PV. Consequences: (1) V2.1 3.3 defines the set 'per checkpoint (P0, PL, PV, PC)', so the PC members cannot be learned and every governing run's E-04 at PC fails or is UNKNOWN (row 7). (2) V2.1 3.4 measures P-L2 at PC and P-L3 up to V1; both become unmeasurable, which gives 'UNKNOWN', so no candidate qualifies and E-03 is a class-A FAIL. (3) Without HOST_DEFAULT_MAP, BA-08 V3 section 11 rule 5 makes the comparison 'UNKNOWN (O5 path)'. AR2-16 makes TOL_SCALE-dependent scenarios DRAFT with K-3 and does not limit this to governing runs. (4) E4-LEARN-R1 has MODE LEARNING while LK-* has CHARACTERIZATION_RUN, although AR2-11 calls both characterization. V2.4 gates 'the first LEARNING run' on REVIEWED, and md 2.1 requires a LOCK_MODE pin for 'every learning run', which E4-LEARN does not carry. BA04-F01 had named these runs ('LK-LM1/2-PROPS/CONFLICT, E4-LEARN-R1 ... EVM_VERSION = NONE').
findings.required_fix: Before the catalog can be a candidate, obtain an Architect ruling that reconciles AR2-11's order with V2.1 3.2, 8 and 14. For example: extend RECORDED_NOT_ENFORCED to E-12 phases A and C, and record the S-1..S-3 comparisons without adjudication, in the pre-EVM characterization runs so that they reach PC and V1; or reorder the learning chain. Then re-declare the six runs to match the ruling: no reference to a pinned EVM, a non-adjudicated or conditional product outcome, and pins and blockers per md section 2 (HOST_DEFAULT_MAP and K-3, or a stated exemption). Set STATUS to DRAFT until then, set E4-LEARN MODE to CHARACTERIZATION_RUN, and make the md 2.1 LOCK_MODE row match the per-candidate design.

findings.evidence: md 5.2: 'Every governing host scenario X (reach P0 or later) has one dry-run scenario WU-DRY-X ... There are 145 of them ... no per-family reduction is used.' The JSON has 156 GOVERNING scenarios with REACH in P0..CP. The 11 listed (REACH PW, PV or CP) have no WU-DRY, which contradicts AR2-42 ('criterio por escenario ... sin reduccion por familia'). The six non-governing CP runs also enforce E-11M (E11M is exercised and not exempted) and have no dry run either. Every WU-DRY of a CP-reach scenario (for example WU-DRY-CL-CLEAN-FX1F-F0) declares REACH CP and EXPECTED_EVENTS MUTATION (A) 'exactly the EXPECTED_MUTATION_EVENT_SET of the pinned frozen EVM for f(plan)', with TUPLE FULL_BASELINE_TUPLE, EVM_VERSION NONE and PIN_SLOTS only FIXTURE_INSTANCE. Without the E-04 set, LOCK_MODE and EVM such a run is refused at P0 or PL, or aborts at PV, so it never exercises the post-PV window that V2.1 13.1 measures ('no assembly-load event occurs inside the governed window'). Section 213.1 also reports '219 propios + 151 dry runs', but the catalog has 225 + 145.

findings.evidence: U-3: INJECTIONS Wr-A at X3, TARGET S3, outcome 'preceding run: O4', but EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS lists only {'UNDO': ...}, CONTROLS_EXERCISED is [] and INJECTION_COORDINATE is NONE. U-4 (fault at X4, target S3, O5) and U-5 (CANARY_LOAD at X7, target E11M, O7) have the same shape. Under the md section 4 default, S3 and E11M are therefore expected PASS. NC-E11M-PC, which uses the same X7 canary load, declares 'E10: FAIL at PC (the canary module changes the PC snapshot)', which AR2-25 mandates, but U-5 does not. U-1: PLAN 'stops before T_M (as AB-AFTER-PREPARE-W)', yet INJECTIONS [] and DELIBERATE_VIOLATION_FLAG NO, whereas AB-AFTER-PREPARE-W declares HARNESS_FAULT 'stop before T_M' with flag YES; AR2-20 requires flag YES with a target where a fault is injected. U-6b is GOVERNING with REACH PV and outcome 'the host exception (origin recorded; no product outcome is declared)', although a Commit() exception gives T_M = FAILED and 17.2 rows 3/4 (O2/O6 by CER-ABV). EA1-READONLY-OPENS has REACH CP, LP-CP (with COMMIT x1), EVM and HOST_DEFAULT_MAP pins and K-3, but outcome 'NONE (no commit in the measured interval)'. md line 112 states 'Every expected outcome is an exact O1..O7, NONE, a declared conditional of section 3, or a non-governing result.'
findings.required_fix: U-3, U-4, U-5: declare the target result (S3 difference; S3 UNKNOWN; E11M FAIL at PC together with the E-10 FAIL at PC collateral), list the controls in CONTROLS_EXERCISED, and set INJECTION_COORDINATE. U-1: declare the stop injection with flag YES and a target, as AB-AFTER-PREPARE-W does. U-6b: give O2/O6 by CER-ABV, or classify it as non-governing with a stated reason. EA1: declare the product outcome of the committing run (O3), or make the run non-product. Then correct md line 112.

findings.location: WR-F-X7 and WR-G-X7 (GROUP 'SC-A', GROUPS_SERVED [SC-A, KS, E8]); GROUP of WR-F/G-X5, X6 and the -EV variants; md section 5 group counts (SC-A 59, SC-B 32)
findings.claim: The V3 regrouping of the read-set writers leaves SC-B with no X7 cell for Wr-F or Wr-G, contrary to V2.1 10.8. It also labels E-08 detections at X5..X7 as SC-A, whose content is designed detection at X1..X4.
findings.evidence: In V2, WR-F-X7 and WR-G-X7 had GROUP SC-B and GROUPS_SERVED ['SC-B']. In V3 they have GROUP 'SC-A' and GROUPS_SERVED ['SC-A','KS','E8'], and no scenario for Wr-F or Wr-G at X7 serves SC-B. V2.1 10.8: 'group SC-B includes an X7 scenario per writer (10.6) that reports what the tail log delivered for the injected change'. V2.2 PA-1.3: SC-B is '... residual cells; the X7 tail log is reported here as evidence', and SC-A is 'semantic comparison S-2, S-3 and designed detection at X1..X4'. The X5..X7 cells of these writers are detected by E-08 at PC, and E-08's only group is E8 (PA-1.2). Nothing in AR2-14 asks for the regrouping. Meanwhile the X7 cells of Wr-A..Wr-E serve SC-B without any SC-B control or declared evidence group (see BA04V3-08).
findings.required_fix: Set the GROUP of WR-F/G-X5..X7 and their EV variants to E8, their target control's group. Declare SC-B in EVIDENCE_GROUPS_DECLARED for every X7 cell (tail-log evidence) so that each writer A..G has an X7 cell serving SC-B. Recompute the md group counts and BA-02b section 4.

findings.location: NC-S5-O6 (PLAN_OR_INPUT, EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS, EXPECTED_PRODUCT_OUTCOME, CONDITIONAL_EXPECTATION_RULE); md section 3
findings.claim: No declared control is guaranteed to abort the only S-5 negative control. It relies on E-12 phase A adjudicating an event on a pre-existing layer, which is outside the phase-A domain. If nothing aborts, the run commits and the expected O6 cannot happen.
findings.evidence: PLAN: 'at Y1 the harness changes the colour of a pre-existing layer of the PRE_COMMAND_STATE_RECORD through an OpenCloseTransaction ...; the change emits a phase-A event and the run aborts before Commit()'. EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS has E12A 'CONDITIONAL (CER-WIT): FAIL when the witness records the event delivered' and S5 only. V2.2 PA-10 and BA-08 V3 section 5 define the phase-A domain as the plan-time protected set (SL-S, SL-P, the pre-existing containers of SL-C) plus objects created inside T_M; 'events outside it are recorded and not adjudicated'. A pre-existing layer belongs to none of these. Nor is it in the E-08 read-set, which is SL-S (and SL-P for Wr-F) per BA-08 V3 section 4 and AR2-14. Nor is it an SL-Y element in FX-1F (all toggles off, no dimensions). The CER is also conditional, so if the witness records no delivery nothing aborts before Commit(); the run then follows 17.2 rows 5-8, ABORT-VERIFY never runs, and CER-PERSIST ('independent post-abort read') has nothing to resolve. The E-06 result for an OpenCloseTransaction is exactly the unresolved question of E6-C4 (EXPLORATORY), yet the default rule expects PASS. CER-PERSIST is not in md section 3 'The declared rules' or in the JSON CONDITIONAL_EXPECTATION_RULES. BA-02b V3 lists NC-S5-O6 as the only S-5 negative control.
findings.required_fix: Name the exact object changed, and make the abort unconditional through a control whose domain covers it. For example, choose a member of the E-08 read-set or an SL-Y element compared by S-1, and declare that FAIL at PV. Make E12A consistent with PA-10: PASS or not adjudicated for an out-of-domain object. Declare E-06, or mark the scenario BLOCKED_BY E6-C4. Register CER-PERSIST in md section 3 and in the JSON rules. If no out-of-undo-scope write on an adjudicated object exists, record a sealed reason that S-5 cannot be violated in a governing run.

findings.location: JSON CONDITIONAL_EXPECTATION_RULES; md section 3 (lines 66-71); EA2-DEFERRED-EVENTS
findings.claim: The conditional-rule registry is inconsistent between the two files. CER-A2 partly resolves delivery from the E-12 log, which AR2-12 forbids. EA2's O7 branch does not declare the E-12 phase C FAIL it implies.
findings.evidence: The JSON registry has 3 rules (CER-ABV, CER-WIT, CER-SIL). md section 3 lists 4 (adds CER-A2). CER-PERSIST, used by NC-S5-O6, is in neither. CER-A2 is 'resolved offline from the sealed phase-C log and the I-14 witness', but AR2-12 says every rule that depends on 'evento entregado' is resolved from the I-14 witness, 'nunca con el log del propio E-12'. EA2's CER gives 'a deferred event in phase C => O7', which means E12C FAIL (17.2 row 7, EVT_C). EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS lists only A2, so the default expects E12C PASS. A2 is given as 'PASS ... ; CHARACTERIZED_DIFFERENT otherwise', which is a group verdict, not a control result (V2.1 26.1: PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN).
findings.required_fix: Register the same set of rules (including CER-A2 and CER-PERSIST) in both files. Resolve CER-A2 from the I-14 witness only. In EA2, declare E12C conditional (FAIL on the O7 branch) and express A2 as a control result (FAIL), leaving CHARACTERIZED_DIFFERENT as the group verdict.

findings.location: GROUPS_SERVED and EVIDENCE_GROUPS_DECLARED of 65 scenarios; md section 1 GROUPS_SERVED row; BA-02b V3 section 1 rule 1
findings.claim: GROUPS_SERVED is not derived by the AR2-08 rule in 65 scenarios, yet both artifacts state that it is.
findings.evidence: Recomputing union(affectedGroups(CONTROLS_EXERCISED)) plus EVIDENCE_GROUPS_DECLARED gives these mismatches: Q-* (25) and OU-* (11) serve Q or OU with EVIDENCE_GROUPS_DECLARED []; EV-L-* (16) serve E12-L with []; WR-A/D/E-X7, WR-A/D/E/F/G-X8, WR-B-X0, WR-B-X7 and WR-C-X7 serve SC-B with CONTROLS_EXERCISED [S2,S3] and []; PW-CLONE-WRONG-TYPE serves PW-CLONE without CLONE in CONTROLS_EXERCISED; PR-CLOSURE-COMPLETENESS serves PR-REC with no control, and its GROUP is PR-REC (a CONTROL group, PA-1.3) with verdict 'PASS (EVIDENCE_COMPLETE)', the residual of F24(d). md section 1 says 'derived by the normative rule of BA-02b V3 section 1 (AR2-08)'. BA-02b V3 says 'BA-04 V3 derives the field with this rule, so sections 2 and 3 agree by construction'.
findings.required_fix: Fill EVIDENCE_GROUPS_DECLARED for every evidence contribution (Q, OU, E12-L, SC-B tail-log cells). Add CLONE to PW-CLONE-WRONG-TYPE, or drop PW-CLONE from its GROUPS_SERVED. Give PR-CLOSURE-COMPLETENESS a consistent group and verdict kind (Q with EVIDENCE_COMPLETE, or PR-REC with a control verdict). Then add a mechanical check that the field equals the derivation.

findings.location: md section 4 log profiles (LP-P0, LP-PW, LP-PV, LP-LEARN) and TUPLE_REQUIREMENTS row; EXPECTED_LOG_RECORD_SET of AB-AFTER-PREPARE-W, PR-SOURCE-SWAP-NEG-COPY, PW-IMPORT-PARTIAL-FAIL, U-1, NC-WU-FOREIGN, KS-SL1-TX-MISMATCH, KS-SL4-NEG-DET; the 32 Q-* and E6-C* TUPLE_REQUIREMENTS
findings.claim: Several declared log profiles do not match the scenario's reach. The profile assigned to four abort-after-PREPARE-W scenarios has no ABORT_VERIFY record, although their expectation or CER reads that record. One tuple profile is undefined.
findings.evidence: LP-PW = 'LP-PR plus REOBSERVATION ...; MANIFEST x1; CHECKPOINT x1 (PP)', with no ABORT_VERIFY. It is used by AB-AFTER-PREPARE-W ('S5: PASS (ABORT-VERIFY match)'), PR-SOURCE-SWAP-NEG-COPY and PW-IMPORT-PARTIAL-FAIL (both CER-ABV 'resolved offline from the sealed ABORT-VERIFY record'), and U-1 (LP-EVID over LP-PW, CER-ABV). KS-SL1-TX-MISMATCH and KS-SL4-NEG-DET abort at seam entry but use LP-PV, which requires 'SEAM_CALL x1 per seam call of f(plan)' and 'CHECKPOINT x2 (PS, PV)'. V2.2 PA-3 condition 3 and V2.1 26.1 compare the observed log with the declared set.
findings.required_fix: Add a profile, or per-scenario deltas, for stop-after-PREPARE-W (LP-PW plus ABORT x1 and ABORT_VERIFY x1), for refusal before subscription, and for abort at seam entry. Add the LOCK record to LP-LEARN if the lock is held. Define QUALIFICATION_TUPLE in md section 4.

findings.location: PR-SOURCE-SWAP-NEG-COPY, EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS
findings.claim: The LIBF result expected on a copy re-hash mismatch contradicts the authority the scenario cites.
findings.evidence: Declared: 'LIBF': 'FAIL detected by the pre-import copy re-hash; the second import does not start'. V2.1 19.1, Element table, UNKNOWN row: '... the copy hash differs from the record ...'. The scenario cites 19.1 as its authority, and PR-TORN-READ correctly uses UNKNOWN for the analogous acquisition case.

findings.location: PW-CLONE-WRONG-TYPE (FIXTURE FX-1F-XREF-HOMONYM, INPUT_STATUS FIXTURE_SPEC_DEFINED, STATUS SEALED_PENDING_PIN_CANDIDATE)
findings.claim: The chosen wrong-type variant cannot be built as specified, yet the scenario claims a defined fixture and carries no blocker.
findings.evidence: BA-08 V3 section 12 defines FX-1F-XREF-HOMONYM as 'FX-1F plus a resolved attached external reference named as one required block', and its Templates paragraph says each fixture contains 'the required library blocks as imported by that drawing'. Section 7 lists the FX-1F required set (post, plate, beam, and celosia). A mirror of FX-1F requires the same names, so every required name is already a normal block definition in FX-1F. Block-table names are unique, so no xref can take that name unless the existing definition is removed or renamed first. That changes the template, and possibly the source read-set, and is not 'FX-1F plus'. V2.1 11.3 REJECT needs 'the pre-existing name is ... an external-reference ... record'.
findings.required_fix: Specify a constructible wrong-type variant, such as an FX-IMP base whose absent required name is taken by a resolved xref (then K-8 applies), or an explicit rename step with its effect on the read-set stated. Set INPUT_STATUS, BLOCKED_BY and STATUS accordingly.

findings.location: REPETITION of EA2-DEFERRED-EVENTS; md section 4 repetition rule CLEAN; BA-10 V3 section 2 (PARAM-03 combination rule, run-count expression)
findings.claim: The CLEAN repetition rule is assigned to a scenario that is not CL-CLEAN, and BA-10 V3 divides n by 9 while the catalog has 8 CL-CLEAN scenarios. The PARAM-03 sample can then fall short of n. The implementer report also misstates the scenario counts.
findings.evidence: BA-04 CLEAN rule: 'ceil(PARAM-03 n / number of CL-CLEAN scenarios)'. The JSON has 8 CL-CLEAN-* scenarios, but CLEAN is assigned to 9 (the 8 plus EA2-DEFERRED-EVENTS). BA-10 V3: 'The sample is drawn from the CL-CLEAN-* scenarios (9 scenarios in BA-04 V3) ... each CL-CLEAN scenario runs max(N_strict, ceil(n / 9))' and 'CLEAN 9 scenarios'. When ceil(n/9) dominates, 8*ceil(n/9) < n is possible (for example n = 59 gives 56), so PARAM-03's 'n clean governing runs' drawn from CL-CLEAN is not guaranteed. Section 213.1 says '370 escenarios (219 propios + 151 dry runs)', while the catalog has 225 own scenarios and 145 WU-DRY (151 is the NON_GOVERNING_BY_DESIGN total).
findings.required_fix: Either count EA2 in the clean sample and name it in the rule, or give EA2 its own rule. Make the divisor equal to the actual number of sample scenarios in both BA-04 and BA-10. Correct the counts in section 213 through the next decisions entry.

findings.location: KS-SL1-TX-MISMATCH, EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS 'E06'
findings.claim: The AR2-25 collateral is declared at a sampling point that the contract does not define.
findings.evidence: Declared: 'E06': 'FAIL at the SL-1 sampling point (a second transaction is open)'. The V2.1 4.2 expected-count table defines only P0, PL, before and after each AUTH-12 call or import, PS, PV, after Commit/Abort and VERIFY. The seam fails PRE-WRITE and 'the caller aborts', so whether PV is reached, and at which point the count of 2 is sampled, is not determined.
findings.required_fix: Name the defined sampling point where E-06 fails (for example after Abort() and disposal, if the nested harness transaction is still open), or add the sampling point through BA-08/BA-06 with its authority.

findings.location: DELIBERATE_VIOLATION_FLAG / TARGET_NEGATIVE_CONTROL of PR-SOURCE-SWAP-MODIFY/DELETE, PW-CLONE-BASE/CASE/NESTED/SYMTAB/WRONG-TYPE, AB-AFTER-PREPARE-W, AB-AFTER-MUTATION, KS-*, and the residual WR cells; md section 1
findings.claim: The catalog pairs flag YES with target NONE for designed stimuli. V2.1 26.1 defines neither the convention nor this combination, and the combination distorts the coverage matrix.
findings.evidence: V2.1 26.1: DELIBERATE_VIOLATION_FLAG is 'YES when the scenario deliberately violates a control', and TARGET_NEGATIVE_CONTROL is 'the control the violation must be detected by (empty if the flag is NO)'. The NOTEs of PR-SOURCE-SWAP-MODIFY and PW-CLONE-* say that no control is violated or expected to fail. Because a YES run is not a 'clean governing run' (V2.1 1.3), BA-02b V3 lists only CL-CLEAN-FXIMP-FP as CLONE's clean governing coverage and lists PW-CLONE-CASE as a CLONE 'secondary channel'. md section 1 does not define the convention.
findings.required_fix: Either set the flag to NO for designed stimuli and add a DESIGNED_STIMULUS field, or define the YES+NONE convention normatively in md section 1 and in BA-02b rule 3, so that clean and negative coverage are computed correctly.

findings.location: PR-REC-CLOSURE-UNKNOWN (L-VAR-PROXY) and PW-CLONE-BASE (L-VAR-DIFF): TUPLE_REQUIREMENTS, PIN_SLOTS, BLOCKED_BY
findings.claim: The variant libraries are scenario-specific tuple fields, but no pin slot or record fixes their hash, and their dependence on the census is not declared as a blocker.
findings.evidence: TUPLE_REQUIREMENTS: 'FULL_BASELINE_TUPLE except the block-library field, which is the declared VARIANT library L-VAR-PROXY ... (its SHA-256 is a scenario-specific tuple field)'. PIN_SLOTS contains only FIXTURE_INSTANCE@FX-1F (or @FX-IMP) plus E04 and LOCK_MODE. V2.1 26.1 FIXTURE covers 'the scratch template, private library copy and manifest, by hash', and AR2-16/AR2-17 make fixture instances pin slots. BA-08 V3 section 12 marks L-VAR-DIFF and L-VAR-PROXY 'content depends on the census (K-2)'. PR-REC-CLOSURE-UNKNOWN is SEALED_PENDING_PIN_CANDIDATE with BLOCKED_BY [].
findings.required_fix: Add FIXTURE_INSTANCE@L-VAR-PROXY and @L-VAR-DIFF (or an equivalent library pin) and register them in BA-11 3.1. Either declare the K-2 dependency (blocker or pin source) or state why the variant content is independent of the census.

findings.location: section 2.1, HOST_DEFAULT_MAP row; catalog content
findings.claim: Every other pin names the catalog scenarios it comes from; HOST_DEFAULT_MAP is required by 137 scenarios and has no source scenario in the catalog.
findings.evidence: md 2.1 gives the source as 'host-default attributes derived from non-governing evidence (BA-08 V3, PH2-OR-1)', and BA-11 V3 3.1 says 'non-governing characterization'. By contrast, E04_ADMITTED_SET is sourced from E4-LEARN-R1-*, LOCK_MODE from LK-* and EVM_FROZEN from EV-L-*. No scenario in the 370 characterizes the host-default attributes. BA-08 V3 section 11 rule 5 makes every such comparison UNKNOWN until the pin exists.
findings.required_fix: Add a non-governing characterization scenario, or scenarios, that produce the HOST_DEFAULT_MAP pin record, with its place in the AR2-11 sequence. Alternatively, record that the PH2-OR-1 ruling will define it and carry the dependency as an open item in md section 7.

findings.location: Q-I14-X, Q-I14-Y, Q-I14-SILENT (FIXTURE NONE, REACH NONE, PLAN_OR_INPUT)
findings.claim: The qualifications on which CER-WIT and CER-SIL depend measure at product-run coordinates while declaring no fixture and no product run. What they measure therefore may not correspond to the governing context.
findings.evidence: Q-I14-Y: 'a writer at Y0, Y1 and Y2 produces its intended effect through T_M', where Y0..Y2 are defined relative to PS, the last seam write and the sealing of VERIFY_ELEMENT_LIST (md 6.1). Q-I14-X covers 'each writer ... at each position X0..X8', and X0..X8 are defined by Commit(), V0, the pass reads, V1 and CP (V2.1 10.6). Q-I14-SILENT reports 'AVAILABLE or NOT_AVAILABLE ... per coordinate (Y0, Y1, Y2, X1..X6)'. All three declare FIXTURE NONE and REACH NONE. CER-SIL makes 17 governing scenarios runnable, and CER-WIT resolves 70 expectations, from these records.
findings.required_fix: Give the three qualifications a fixture and a harness run that reaches the coordinates (with pins as needed). Alternatively, declare the harness emulation of each coordinate and the reason its result transfers to the governed run.

rulings.item: AR2-11 learning chain against E-12 phase-A fail-closed (BA04V3-01)
rulings.recommendation: The Architect should add a closed ruling: during the pre-EVM characterization runs (E4-LEARN-R1-*, LK-*), E-12 phases A and C are RECORDED_NOT_ENFORCED, and the S-1..S-3 comparisons are recorded but not adjudicated, so that these runs reach PV, V1 and PC. Their product outcome is then declared as not adjudicated (a PROVISIONAL, non-governing outcome), with no EVM, HOST_DEFAULT_MAP or K-3 dependency. BA-04 must not become a candidate before this ruling.
rulings.reasoning: AR2-11 exempts only E-03 and E-04, while V2.1 3.2 keeps E-12 fail-closed. With no EVM, every mutation event is unattributable, so the runs abort at PV. The PC members of the E-04 admitted set (V2.1 3.3, per checkpoint) and P-L2/P-L3 (V2.1 3.4, measured up to PC and V1) could then never be observed. The chain would yield LK = FAIL, a class-A FALSE, and an unobtainable E04 pin, and 156 and 163 scenarios depend on these pins.

rulings.item: PH2D-5 / NC-S5-O6 and CER-PERSIST (BA04V3-06)
rulings.recommendation: Accept the CER-PERSIST NOT_RUNNABLE branch only after the scenario names an object inside a control's adjudication domain whose change aborts the run unconditionally before Commit() (an E-08 read-set member, or an S-1-compared element), with that FAIL declared and CER-PERSIST registered. If no write outside the undo scope on such an object exists, record for S-5 a sealed reason that it cannot be deliberately violated in a governing run, as for E-01 and E-13.
rulings.reasoning: A pre-existing layer is outside the phase-A domain (V2.2 PA-10; BA-08 V3 section 5) and outside the E-08 read-set. As written, nothing guarantees an abort, and without an abort ABORT-VERIFY never runs. NC-S5-O6 is the only S-5 negative control in BA-02b V3, so a scenario whose outcome is undetermined leaves S-5 uncovered.

rulings.item: NOT_RUNNABLE outcomes (NC-E12C, CER-SIL scenarios, NC-S5-O6)
rulings.recommendation: Rule that a scenario resolved NOT_RUNNABLE leaves its coverage cell uncovered. The BA-02b state for that control is NOT_EVALUATED, never MET or PASS, until a runnable instance exists.
rulings.reasoning: AR2-12 already says a NOT_RUNNABLE NC-E12C 'does not count as NC-E12C coverage'. BA-02b V3 still marks the E12C, S5 and silent-isolation rows MET_IN_DRAFT whatever the runnability, which would allow check 2 of V2.1 31 to pass on an isolation that was never achieved.

rulings.item: Per-scenario warm-up dry runs (AR2-42 scope; BA04V3-02)
rulings.recommendation: Confirm that WU-DRY is required for every scenario whose run enters the governed window, including the 11 evidence-group scenarios and the non-governing CP characterization runs. Also confirm that dry runs carry the pin slots needed to traverse the window, or rule explicitly that in dry runs E-03, E-04 and E-12 are recorded and not enforced.
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 13.1 defines the coverage criterion per scenario, 'inside the governed window', and AR2-42 forbids per-family reduction. A dry run that is refused at P0 or aborts at PV for lack of a pin measures nothing after PV, which is where the product's lazy loads (commit, verify) happen.

rulings.item: Designed-stimulus flag convention (BA04V3-14)
rulings.recommendation: Designed stimuli (source swap, clone variants, induced seam failures, residual scanner cells) should use DELIBERATE_VIOLATION_FLAG = NO plus a DESIGNED_STIMULUS field. If the catalog keeps YES with TARGET NONE, it must be defined normatively in BA-04 section 1 and in BA-02b rule 3, together with its effect on the 'clean governing run' definition (V2.1 1.3).
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 26.1 ties YES to the violation of a control that the target must detect. The current mixture makes BA-02b report a single clean scenario for CLONE_POLICY_VERIFIED, and a clone variant as a 'secondary channel'.

rulings.item: HOST_DEFAULT_MAP source as it concerns BA-04 (PH2-OR-1; BA04V3-16)
rulings.recommendation: When ruling on PH2-OR-1, require BA-04 to carry a named non-governing characterization scenario as the source of the HOST_DEFAULT_MAP pin record, placed after the LOCK_MODE selection and before any governing run that uses S-1..S-3.
rulings.reasoning: Every other pin kind has a source scenario in the catalog. 137 governing scenarios depend on HOST_DEFAULT_MAP, and BA-08 V3 section 11 rule 5 makes every such comparison UNKNOWN until it is pinned.

findings.location: BA-05 V3 section 3.3, SV-06 (line 863), SV-07 (864), SV-10 (867) and SV-11 (868); section 3.1 line 821 and the TOL_SCALE row (line 829); gen.py lines 503-515 (semanticVectors 'rule' texts, copied into the JSON)
findings.claim: BA-05 states tolerance values, and the expected results of four normative semantic vectors depend on them. This contradicts AR2-35 and BA-05's own section 3.1, and brings back the BA-05 -> BA-08 dependency that BA-11 V3 declares broken.
findings.evidence: Line 821: 'The tolerance values live only in BA-08 V3 section 10 ... this section names the slots (AR2-35)'. Yet SV-06 says '5e-10 <= TOL_LENGTH = 1e-9 in', SV-10 says 'TOL_ANGLE = 1e-9 rad' and SV-11 says 'TOL_NORMAL = 1e-9 rad'. The EQUAL/DIFFERENT results of SV-06, SV-07, SV-10 and SV-11 hold only for those values (verified: 10.0000000005 - 10 = 5.0000004e-10 and 10.000000002 - 10 = 2.0000002e-9). BA-11 V3 line 51 says 'the tolerance values live only in BA-08 ... BA-08 depends on BA-05 ... not the reverse'. Line 54 seals BA-05 before BA-08, and line 64 gives BA-05 DEPENDS_ON = BA-01 plus the census. BA-04 V3 Q-FPSPEC-VECTORS expects 'every semantic result reproduced' from BA-05 3.3. If BA-08 section 10 changes a value, the sealed BA-05 vectors become wrong and no cascade fires. The TOL_SCALE row also restates BA-08's status ('UNSET, no authority'), which goes stale the same way.
findings.required_fix: Take every numeric tolerance value out of BA-05 and out of the JSON 'rule' texts. Two options: (a) write SV-06, SV-07, SV-10 and SV-11 in slot units (for example persisted = expected + 0.5*TOL_LENGTH gives EQUAL, + 2*TOL_LENGTH gives DIFFERENT), with the binary64 instances produced from the sealed BA-08 section 10 values by the Q-FPSPEC-VECTORS harness; or (b) move the numeric instances into BA-08, which depends on BA-05. Make the TOL_SCALE row say 'value and status: BA-08 V3 section 10'. Confirm that BA-11 DEPENDS_ON stays acyclic.

findings.location: BA-05 V3 section 3.1 table (lines 825-829) and section 3.1.1 ANGLE_DIFF_LE (line 841); BA-08 V3 section 10 lines 161-162
findings.claim: The slots BA-05 names are not the slots BA-08 defines, and the angle normalization is defined twice with different formulas.
findings.evidence: BA-08 V3 line 161 defines TOL_TEXT_HEIGHT and TOL_DIM (both = TOL_LENGTH). BA-05 never names them and routes text heights and dimension points to TOL_LENGTH. V2.2 PA-9 gives 'tolerances and normalizations' to the kind baseline. BA-08 line 162 defines NORM_ANGLE as NormalizePi to (-pi, pi] (RackSourceTransformFactsV2.cs:255-261 at 3375aadb), then the wrapped difference. BA-05 line 841 defines ANGLE_DIFF_LE as d = abs(a - b) mod 2pi, then min(d, 2pi - d). The two agree in exact arithmetic but are separate normative texts, and neither says which governs.
findings.required_fix: In section 3.1, name exactly BA-08's slots for each compared value class (TOL_TEXT_HEIGHT for text heights, TOL_DIM for dimension points). Define ANGLE_DIFF_LE by reference to BA-08's NORM_ANGLE, so the normalization is written once, in BA-08 (PA-9).

findings.location: Section 2.3, STATE_MEMBER table, memberKey row (line 640); gen.py line 156 (SCHEMAS) and line 467 (member())
findings.claim: The document's field table gives the wrong separator in memberKey. It does not match the normative registry or the vectors, although section 2.3 says the tables are generated from SCHEMAS.
findings.evidence: The document has 'category/recordKind/expectedName'. SCHEMAS and the EV-62/EV-64 streams use 'category|recordKind|expectedName' (for example 'memberKey=S23:CLOSURE|BLOCK|POSTE_3X3'). A mechanical comparison of all 41 document tables against the JSON schemas finds this as the only difference. An implementer who follows the document produces EV-62 = feccb866... instead of the normative 53e63bb0....
findings.required_fix: Escape the pipe in the Markdown table (for example a code span or \|), and check mechanically that every table cell is identical to SCHEMAS.

findings.location: Section 2.1.2 (line 56); gen.py RB_KIND_RANGES (lines 43-50) and rb_kind (lines 54-60)
findings.claim: The RB code table is not byte-determinate. Code 5 is declared UNKNOWN in the prose but digested as a string by the normative encoder. Point-valued codes are typed as double, although a managed ResultBuffer holds a Point3d under those codes.
findings.evidence: The prose says 'Unsupported ... (5, 105, 320-369, 390-399, 480-481, 1005 as handle)', but the range 0-9 is 'string', and rb_kind(5) returns 'string' (probed). The encoder therefore emits '{RB code=5 value=S2:1F}': a database handle inside an exact digest, against the V2.1 28.1 exclusions. Codes 10-18 and 1010-1013 (and other point codes such as 110-112 and 210) carry Point3d values in a .NET TypedValue. The table says double, and the reference encoder raises TypeError on them, which is neither a digest nor UNKNOWN. Impact is limited: the product writes only DxfCode.Text (RackBlockData.cs:38, ProjectVariablesData.cs:119-120, CustomPropertiesData.cs:135), so this concerns foreign Xrecords under the keys the read-set reads.
findings.required_fix: Split the range to 0-4 and 6-9 (or special-case 5 as UNKNOWN in rb_kind). Declare the point-valued codes either as an inline POINT3D value or as UNKNOWN. Add vectors for code 5 (UNKNOWN) and for a Point3d code with the chosen result.

findings.location: Section 2.3, lines 68 and 285-298, and the ENTITY_* tables; section 2.5
findings.claim: The rule that maps a host entity to an ENTITY_* record type is not defined, and the choice changes the result.
findings.evidence: The mapping could be by DXF name, by exact runtime class, or by a subclass ('is') test, and these give different answers. AttributeReference and AttributeDefinition derive from DBText. MInsertBlock and Table derive from BlockReference, and MInsertBlock has DXF name INSERT. RotatedDimension and AlignedDimension share DXF name DIMENSION. Depending on the rule, an MInsertBlock or Table in a library block or a pre-existing homologue becomes ENTITY_INSERT (a lossy digest) or UNKNOWN. No vector separates the rules.
findings.required_fix: Give a closed table from the exact host runtime class (or RXClass name) to the record type, with every other class UNKNOWN. Add a vector for a subclass or DXF-name collision (for example an MInsertBlock) that must be UNKNOWN.

findings.location: ENTITY_INSERT.dynamicProperties (line 297); ENTITY_ROTATED_DIMENSION.overrides and ENTITY_ALIGNED_DIMENSION.overrides (lines 417, 455); section 2.4 (line 734)
findings.claim: How the two map-valued fields are extracted from the host is not specified, and the overrides field conflicts with the coverage boundary.
findings.evidence: dynamicProperties: the spec does not say which entries count (all, writable only, or visible only). The product writes only non-ReadOnly properties (LateralHeaderDrawer.cs:430-436), and BA-08 V3 section 11 rule 2 speaks of 'writable' ones. A host collection can repeat a name among read-only entries; this is host behaviour that the census must confirm. If it does, the duplicate-key rule turns every such reference UNKNOWN. The mapping from host value types (Int16, string, Point2d/Point3d) to TYPED_VALUE kinds, including STRING versus NAME, is not stated. overrides: the source is undefined (the entity's ACAD DSTYLE XData, or effective value compared with the style). The two readings differ when an override equals the style value. The product sets 8 per-entity overrides whenever the style is not named (LateralHeaderDrawer.cs:362-372; sa2 F05-A04 leaves their storage UNCERTAIN). Meanwhile section 2.4 declares entity XData not fingerprinted.
findings.required_fix: Define the membership of dynamicProperties (for example the writable properties, with duplicates UNKNOWN and disclosed). Add a table from host value type to TYPED_VALUE kind. Define the source of overrides (for example the decoded ACAD DSTYLE XData pairs) and carve that XData out of the 2.4 boundary.

findings.location: STATE_MEMBER.recordKind (line 642); section 2.3 production record types; BA-08 V3 section 6, lines 112 and 114
findings.claim: STATE_MEMBER admits recordKind BINDING, but no record type defines its digest, and the mapping from recordKind to record type is not stated. Two read-set components that BA-08 assigns to the exact layer have no BA-05 record able to carry them.
findings.evidence: V2.1 6 and 11.1 put 'bindings and addresses: per-view RackViewAddress and grouping' into the PRE_COMMAND_STATE_RECORD. BA-08 V3 line 114 marks 'view addresses and grouping' as EXA, and line 112 marks 'the RackCad reference set with class' as EXA (ENUMERATION). BA-05 V3 has no BINDING or view-address record type. ENUMERATION items carry only names or handles, so they cannot carry a class. A PRESENT BINDING member therefore has no defined digest.
findings.required_fix: Either add a record type (for example VIEW_BINDING: owner, rackId, kind, view, section, grouping), or state that addresses are covered by PAYLOAD_EXACT and remove BINDING. Add a recordKind -> record type table. Define how the reference class is carried (for example an ENUMERATION item form 'handle:class', or a record set).

findings.location: ENUMERATION (doc line 546; EV-61, gen.py line 463); NOD_ENTRY objectClass (doc line 536); section 2.1 duplicate rules
findings.claim: Several documented rules are neither enforced by the reference encoder nor pinned by any vector, so a non-conformant I-12 still passes every vector.
findings.evidence: With ordered = 0, 'the producer sorts the items', but 'items' is encoded as seq:string with no sorting (probed: ['b','a'] streams b before a), and EV-61's input is already sorted. The rule that any NOD_ENTRY objectClass other than XRECORD or DICTIONARY is UNKNOWN is not implemented (the enum accepts any string), and nothing checks that 'data' and 'children' are absent where required. The UNKNOWN for a duplicate set member or key is implemented but has no vector.
findings.required_fix: Enforce these rules in the encoder: sort, or reject unsorted input, when ordered = 0; UNKNOWN for another objectClass; conditional absences. Add discriminating vectors: an unsorted ordered = 0 ENUMERATION, a NOD_ENTRY of another class giving UNKNOWN, and a duplicate set member giving UNKNOWN.

findings.location: Section 2.6 (lines 747-750)
findings.claim: The versioning rule says that when a table is 'added or changed' before the seal, 'every existing vector' stays unchanged. That is false for a changed table, and V3 itself contradicts it.
findings.evidence: A changed table changes its own vectors and, through blockDigest and the member digests, every dependent vector (EV-48, EV-49, EV-50, EV-62, EV-64). V3 kept FPSPEC-V1 and yet changed the digests of EV-12 (45a51010 -> 36c09d5b), EV-17 (920c68a4 -> 8c120f36), EV-19 (94c92e2d -> aff99049) and EV-20 (c1e2600c -> 90d3fefb) against the V2 vector file.
findings.required_fix: Say that before the seal, vectors may be added or regenerated while FPSPEC-V1 and the domain separator stay; the vectors are frozen at the seal; any change after the seal is FPSPEC-V2 and a new baseline.

findings.location: Section 3.3, SV-04 (line 861); gen.py lines 498-500
findings.claim: SV-04's input is not a valid Selective design document, so a correct comparator returns a different result token than the vector expects. Its form label is also wrong.
findings.evidence: At 3375aadb, SelectiveBayDocument.Levels is List<SelectiveCellDocument> (SelectivePalletDesignDocument.cs:457), not an integer. The authoritative reader cannot parse {"Levels":2}, so the correct result is 'unparsable record -> UNKNOWN', not UNKNOWN_MEMBER_UNSUPPORTED, and Q-FPSPEC-VECTORS ('every semantic result reproduced') would fail. The premise itself is correct: only the top-level document declares [JsonExtensionData] (line 150). The column is labelled 'typed (parsed JSON)', but the persisted value must be wire text, because the typed form cannot hold the dropped member.
findings.required_fix: Use a valid bay object carrying the unknown member (for example {"Levels":[],"futureKey":1}), label the columns as wire form, and give SV-09 a concrete input.

findings.location: EV-62 (gen.py lines 471-474), EV-64 (lines 479-482), EV-60 (lines 461-462)
findings.claim: The example content of several normative vectors contradicts the specification or the code facts. The encoding is unaffected.
findings.evidence: EV-62 gives the READ_SET BLOCK SEL_FRONTAL_0 the EV-08 TEST_NAME digest (b625be89...), not a DEFINITION_DUMP digest (EV-50 = f51d99b3...). EV-64 gives the LAYER addition the EV-09 TEST_NAME digest (80f92df0...), not the SYMBOL_RECORD_LAYER digest (EV-54 = 08702382...). EV-64 has the import add RACKCAD_ANOTACIONES, while BA-08 V3 line 138 says the seam adds the annotation and dimension layers in T_M, not the import. EV-60 models RACKCAD_CUSTOM_PROPERTIES as a DICTIONARY, but the product writes an Xrecord there (CustomPropertiesData.cs:151-155).
findings.required_fix: Use digests of the right record type from the same file (EV-50, EV-54) and product-consistent keys and structures, or mark these inputs explicitly as synthetic.

findings.location: Section 7, dynamic-trace source table, row T-4 (line 634)
findings.claim: BA-06 V3 cites BA-05 V3 for an 'exact full-database fingerprint before and after', which BA-05 does not define. The cross-reference is broken, and it overstates what the trace can see.
findings.evidence: BA-05 V3 layer 1 is a set of per-record-type digests. Its declared coverage boundary (2.4) excludes XData, extension dictionaries, draw order and more, and any unlisted type yields UNKNOWN (2.5). So a 'full-database' fingerprint is either undefined or UNKNOWN on any drawing with unlisted types, and it is blind to the excluded state.
findings.required_fix: In BA-06, cite the specific BA-05 records and scope used (for example the read-set records of BA-08 V3 section 6) and state the coverage limit. Alternatively, define a scoped database fingerprint in BA-05.

rulings.item: Tolerance values embedded in the normative semantic vectors SV-06, SV-07, SV-10 and SV-11 (N01) versus AR2-35
rulings.recommendation: Rule that BA-05 must not carry numeric tolerance values in any vector or rule text. Numeric semantic instances either become parametric in slot units, generated from the sealed BA-08 section 10 values, or move into BA-08.
rulings.reasoning: AR2-35 and BA-11 V3 2.1 make BA-08 depend on BA-05 and not the reverse. A normative BA-05 result that holds only for BA-08's values is a content dependency under BA-11's own definition, and would escape the cascade.

rulings.item: PA-8 rule 1 'exact numbers' read as the exact JSON number token (SV-12: 1 differs from 1.0)
rulings.recommendation: Accept it and record it as the Architect's interpretation of PA-8.
rulings.reasoning: I-11 keeps unknown members as JsonElement raw text (RackEmbedDocument.ExtensionData is a Dictionary<string, JsonElement>; SelectivePalletDesignDocument.cs:150-151), so a writer that leaves them alone keeps the token. Token equality is the conservative reading that PA-8 rule 2 needs ('drops or alters' fails).

rulings.item: ENTITY_INSERT.blockDigest (@name#digest) versus V2.1 28.1 'nested definitions are referenced by name and have their own digest'
rulings.recommendation: Accept the chained reference as a strengthening, with one required addition: BA-05 must state that UNKNOWN propagates through blockDigest. Any RackCad view definition, or pre-existing homologue, that references a library block holding an unlisted type is then UNKNOWN (O1).
rulings.reasoning: Chaining the digest makes equal digests cover nested content. It also makes the library census a precondition for any digest of a RackCad definition, and section 2.5 bullet 3 ('not refused for its product-drawn content') does not say so.

rulings.item: ABS_DIFF_LE per scalar component (not Euclidean distance) for positions and points
rulings.recommendation: Accept.
rulings.reasoning: This matches GeometryTolerance.AreClose (abs(a-b) <= tol, Vector2D.cs at 3375aadb). The distance rule of V17 LN-3 governs validation of the mirror-line input, not the persisted-versus-expected comparison.

rulings.item: 2.3.4: the contract's PAYLOAD_EXACT 'raw stored bytes' realized as the lossless RB (code, value) sequence
rulings.recommendation: Accept as the Architect's reading of V2.1 28.1, subject to the RB table corrections in N04.
rulings.reasoning: The host stores an Xrecord as a typed ResultBuffer (RackBlockData.cs:35-39). Keeping type codes and chunk boundaries is what F04 required, and it fails closed (UNKNOWN) where UTF-8 cannot represent a chunk.

rulings.item: NB-3 item L-2 (TOL_SCALE) listed in BA-05 section 6 and in the header BLOCKER line
rulings.recommendation: Rule that TOL_SCALE (BA-08 K-3) gates BA-08 and the layer-2 comparisons that need it, but not the BA-05 candidate. The BA-05 candidate gate is the census (L-1) and the review (L-3).
rulings.reasoning: Under AR2-35, BA-05 holds no values, and BA-11 V3 gives BA-05 DEPENDS_ON = BA-01 plus the census. Listing TOL_SCALE as a BA-05 gate recreates the coupling the Architect removed.

- re-anchor after that single IN_USE (h=8, which s9 step 7 and V2.1 29.4 require for 'use'): the step-6 ANCHORED entry must carry a subjectKind/subjectHash (6.1). Subject MANIFEST gives IN_USE->ANCHORED; subject BASELINE gives ANCHORED->ANCHORED. Both are illegal under lines 119/122, so step 5 fails.
- a second IN_USE for the same manifest (V2.1 29.3 and line 126 require one entry per use) is IN_USE->IN_USE, which is illegal.
- two PIN_RECORDED entries followed by one re-anchor: the state machine needs one ANCHORED(PIN) per pin, but step 4 admits only 'the ANCHORED entry that records the anchor of h', and ANCHORED is not among the listed later events. The second entry is a violation.
- a new baseline version (anticipated by AR2-43 and V24-N2) needs BASELINE_RECORDED/BASELINE_APPROVED after index 1. Step 4 excludes both, and 6.1 reserves index 0 for the genesis.
findings.required_fix:
Pick one of two models and state it.
- Model A: record the anchor as its own event (for example ANCHOR_RECORDED, subjectKind ANCHOR, subjectHash = the anchor-record hash, plus anchorRef). A subject's ANCHORED state is then derived: its latest entry index <= h of a verified anchor.
- Model B: allow one ANCHORED entry per covered subject and list them in step 4.
In either model:
- add IN_USE -> IN_USE to the MANIFEST machine;
- define how a new baseline version is recorded (a new log with its own genesis, or legal appended BASELINE_RECORDED/BASELINE_APPROVED entries plus SUPERSEDED for the old version);
- include a worked example in the artifact: genesis -> approval -> anchor -> manifest -> anchor -> IN_USE x2 -> re-anchor -> pins -> re-anchor.

findings.location: s6.2 step 3 (line 104); s6.1 anchorRef (line 96); s9 steps 5-7 (lines 160-162); s10 rows 'an entry removed or reordered' and 'the log rewritten at or before the anchored head' (lines 187-188)
findings.claim: Step 3 takes 'the last anchor' from inside the repository (the anchor record, or the latest ANCHORED entry of the log being verified). It never enumerates the reference of record, the ct21d-baseline/* tags at the remote. A log whose anchored tail was truncated and then rewritten therefore passes. Separately, the ANCHORED entry cannot supply the header hash that step 3 needs.
findings.evidence:
- anchorRef (line 96) holds remote, tag, tag object id, peeled commit SHA and anchored index, but no MANIFEST_CUSTODY_HEADER_HASH. That hash exists only in baseline-anchor.json, and 6.2 does not say at which commit to read it. s9 step 5 says verification uses the tag's peeled commit, but 6.2 never puts this into practice.
- Scenario: anchors A0 (v1, h=1) and A1 (v1-a1, h=6) exist at the remote. An ordinary commit truncates the log to index 2 (the ANCHORED entry of A0) and appends recomputed entries 3'... No reference is rewritten, so this is inside the threat model of V2.1 29.5 and BA-07 s1. It can also happen by accident in a rebase-conflict resolution under docs/WORKFLOW.md.

findings.location: s1(b) (line 21); s2 pin-records row (line 38); s7 PIN machine (line 120); s6.2 step 4 (line 105); cross-reference docs/initiatives/I-52-ct21d-baseline-ba-11-hash-registry-v3.md s2 rule 4 (line 45) and s3.1 (lines 74-84); AR2-16

findings.location: s2.1 PARAM-03 row (line 33); s2.2 PARAM-03 combination rule (line 61); s2.3 count 'CLEAN 9' (line 79)
findings.claim: The clean-run sample that PARAM-03 must deliver is misidentified. It is named 'CL-CLEAN-* scenarios (9 scenarios in BA-04 V3)' and split as ceil(n/9), but only 8 CL-CLEAN-<fixture> scenarios exist. Under the stated membership the sample can fall short of n.
findings.evidence:
- In the BA-04 V3 JSON, the IDs that match CL-CLEAN-* are FX1F-F0, FX1F-P, FX1F-FP, FX2F-ALL, FX4F-ALL, FXANN-FP, FXDIM-FP, FXIMP-FP and CL-CLEANUP-CHECK. The last one is group CL with EVIDENCE_REPETITION.
- The 9 scenarios under the CLEAN rule are the 8 CL-CLEAN-<fixture> scenarios plus EA2-DEFERRED-EVENTS (group EA2).
- BA-04 V3 line 87 divides by 'number of CL-CLEAN scenarios', and AR2-28 says 'número de CL-CLEAN'.
- If the sample is the 8 CL-CLEAN-* scenarios, then 8 x ceil(n/9) < n whenever ceil(n/9) > N_strict. Example: p=0.30, alpha=0.10 (N=7) with u=0.03, c=0.95 (n=99) gives 11 runs each, and 88 < 99. Example: N=29 with u=0.01 (n=299) gives 34 runs each, 8 x 34 = 272 < 299, and the k=0 bound is 1-(0.05)^(1/272) = 0.0110 > u.
- The hard-coded 9 also makes a normative value of BA-10 depend on BA-04. BA-04 already depends on BA-10 (BA-11 V3 line 70), while BA-11 V3 line 51 says BA-10 does not depend on BA-04, so this creates a cycle.
findings.required_fix:
- Declare the sample membership explicitly: the 8 CL-CLEAN-<fixture> scenarios, plus EA2-DEFERRED-EVENTS only if its writer-free runs are declared part of the false-rejection sample (V2.1 10.6).
- Write the rule symbolically as max(N_strict, ceil(n/K)), with K = the number of scenarios in the declared sample of the sealed catalog.
- Align BA-04 V3 (the CLEAN rule text and EA2's REPETITION) and the AR2-28 wording.

findings.location: s2.1 PARAM-04 row (line 34); s2.2 PARAM-04 (line 65), read with s2.2 PARAM-01 (lines 40, 50)
findings.claim: MAX_ATTEMPTS is a cap 'm >= 1 on the attempts of a scenario' where 'every attempt counts', but the same sheet now requires N governing runs per scenario. The cap's unit is not reconciled with N, and the verdict rule only covers a scenario with no governing run at all.
findings.evidence:
- Line 40: a scenario 'runs N governing times'. Line 50: 'N counts planned governing runs, not attempts'. Line 65 (2): every attempt counts toward m. Line 65 (4): 'when a scenario reaches m without a governing run, its group verdict is INVALID'.
- Read per scenario, any m < N makes every scenario impossible to complete (for example m = 3 as a retry cap with N = 29).
- A scenario that reaches m with 1 <= k < N governing runs has no stated consequence.
- V2.1 21.3 separates scheduled repeats from retries. The V2 method (r^m <= beta) was implicitly per governing-run slot; V3 dropped it without stating a unit.
findings.required_fix: State the unit. Either m is the maximum number of attempts per planned governing run (per repetition slot; every attempt of that slot counts, contamination included), or it is a per-scenario cap written as N + r, where r is the retry allowance. Also state the outcome when a scenario ends with fewer governing runs than required: the group lacks a required governing run, so it cannot be PASS; apply the V2.1 1.3/1.6 state consistently.

findings.location: s2.2 PARAM-05 rows 'class-defining attributes', 'label' and 'label value' (lines 72-75); s2.1 PARAM-05 row (line 35)
findings.claim: The class-defining attribute set includes 'the other machine-profile fields'. Under V2.1 2.1 those are the machine identity class (the label itself) and the machine's own module entries recorded in the manifest machine layer. The label is therefore circular, and it cannot be computed before manifest capture (EXEC-11). This contradicts AR2-43 and BA-07 V3 §8.
findings.evidence:
- V2.1 2.1 (lines 236-239) has five MACHINE_PROFILE_BOUND rows: OS version and build; machine identity class ('recorded label agreed at baseline'); AutoCAD profile identity with SECURELOAD and TRUSTEDPATHS; and 'the machine's own module entries (drivers, security software) | manifest machine layer'.
- Line 72 names OS, profile, SECURELOAD and TRUSTEDPATHS, then adds 'and the other machine-profile fields'. Only the label and the module entries remain.
- Line 73 hashes 'all the class-defining attributes'.
- AR2-43 requires the label value to come from a machine-attribute observation in a future host gate, fixed before BASELINE_READY. BA-07 V3 s8 says there is no manifest at the baseline. The module entries come from the E-10 enumerations, which need implemented instruments.
- Consequences: BASE-18 would require EXEC-11, and every driver or security-software update would create a new machine class.
findings.required_fix:
- List the class-defining attributes explicitly (for example MachineGuid, OS version and build, AutoCAD profile identity, SECURELOAD, TRUSTEDPATHS).
- Exclude the machine identity class field itself and the manifest module entries; the module entries stay MACHINE_PROFILE_BOUND tuple fields, checked through the manifest hash.
- State that the observation is a read-only host read that needs no implemented instrument and no manifest.
- Keep the policy as a proposal for confirmation.

findings.location: s6.2 step 4, last sentence (line 105); s10 row 'an entry appended after the anchor and never re-anchored' (line 189); s1 tamper-evidence row (line 25)
findings.claim: The pending-entry coverage check can never report a violation, so the s10 claim that it detects an entry that is never re-anchored is an overclaim. Entries after the last anchor are not tamper-evident until the next anchor; this includes IN_USE entries with runId/tupleRecordHash and PIN_RECORDED entries.
findings.evidence:
- Each anchor's h is the head index at the time of anchoring, so any later anchor covers every entry that existed before it.
- An entry with index <= h' cannot be inserted afterwards without failing step 3.
- An entry that is 'never re-anchored' has no later anchor, so by definition it is PENDING_REANCHOR, which step 4 says is 'not a failure'.
- An edit to a pending entry, with the chain recomputed from h+1, passes steps 1-5, and the next anchor then covers the edited entry.
- V2.1 29.4 only requires re-anchoring 'in the next ... evidence commit', so the exposure window is inherent, but s1 and s10 claim detection.
findings.required_fix:
Choose one:
- make coverage checkable, for example by requiring that every commit changing the custody log after the baseline anchor is itself an anchor commit tagged ct21d-baseline/<version>-a<n>, so an unanchored tail can exist only uncommitted, and have the verifier check this against git history; or
- delete the s10 row and state in s1 that entries after the last anchor are not tamper-evident until the next anchor.

findings.location: s2 independent-copy row (line 42) and closing sentence (line 44); s6.2 step 6 (line 107); anchor placeholder INDEPENDENT_COPY (line 176); s11 N6-1 (line 198)

findings.location: BA-07 V3 s4 'numbers' row (line 61) and s3 step 3 (line 50); BA-10 V3 s2.2 PARAM-05 label (line 73) and PARAM-03 rule (line 61); BA-11 V3 s2.1 (line 51) and rows BA-07/BA-10 (lines 66-67)
findings.claim: The V3 artifacts contain content dependencies that the BA-11 DEPENDS_ON column does not record. One of them forms a cycle.
findings.evidence:
- BA-07 takes its double encoding from BA-05 V3 2.1, but BA-11 lists only BA-01 as a BA-07 dependency.
- The BA-10 PARAM-05 label uses 'the canonical serialization (BA-07 V3 section 4)', but BA-10's DEPENDS_ON omits BA-07.

Removing them is preferred, because a BA-07 -> BA-05 dependency would make BA-07's candidacy wait for the library census, which needs host access.

findings.location: s4 (lines 57-64); s6.1 entryHash (line 98)
findings.claim: The canonical serialization is not fully specified. Every entryHash, the manifest identity, tupleRecordHash and the PARAM-05 label depend on it.
findings.evidence:
- s4 fixes UTF-8, LF, no BOM, sorted keys, integer format and array order. It takes doubles from BA-05, which encodes them as 16 hex digits inside a byte stream, not as JSON numbers.
- s4 does not fix: insignificant whitespace (separators, indentation, trailing LF), string escaping (\uXXXX versus literal characters, '/'), null versus absent fields, or whether a double is a JSON string or a JSON number.
- Two conforming implementations can therefore produce different bytes, and an independent verifier following 6.2 step 1 could report broken entries on an honest log.
findings.required_fix: Adopt a complete canonical form, for example RFC 8785 (JCS) with doubles written as the BA-05 16-hex string, or specify separators, escaping, null handling and the double representation. Add one normative test vector for an entry.

findings.location: s2.3 count labels (line 79), expression (lines 82-83) and table (lines 90-93); decisions §213.2 PH2D-1
findings.claim: The illustrative totals do not follow from the stated expression, and the expression charges N_strict to scenarios that serve only class-A groups.

findings.required_fix: Correct the four totals to 9377, 4562, 2315 and 1352, and record the corrected PH2D-1 figure in the next decisions entry. Split the expression into class-A-only (N_A), mixed (N_strict) and class-B-only (N_B) terms, or state that it assumes N_A >= N_B.

findings.location: s5 closing paragraph (line 124)
findings.claim: The memo tells the Owner that a smaller p, u, alpha or 1-c increases the number of runs 'roughly in proportion'. Under this sheet's own rules that is false for alpha, u and c.
findings.evidence:
- N is about ln(1/alpha)/p, so alpha acts logarithmically: at p=0.10, halving alpha from 0.05 to 0.025 moves N from 29 to 36 (+24%).
- u and c enter only through ceil(n/9), which is below N in all four illustrative rows (7<29, 4<14, 3<7, 2<4). Changing u or c leaves TOTAL unchanged there.
- Only p acts roughly inversely proportionally.
- This paragraph is the Owner's cost input for the decisions.
findings.required_fix: State the actual sensitivities: TOTAL scales roughly with 1/p and logarithmically with 1/alpha, and depends on u and c only when ceil(n/K) exceeds N_strict, in which case only the CLEAN term grows.

findings.location: s2.1 PARAM-02 row (line 32); s2.2 PARAM-02 (line 53); s2.3 term 19 x (N_det + 1)
findings.claim: The extra reference run added for BA10-04 is 'the first learning run of a plan'. That reference cannot serve the determinism-validation repetitions that V2.1 21.7 classifies PARAM-02 for.
findings.evidence:
- V2.1 27.4 requires an identical multiset 'in all governing validation runs'.
- V2.1 27.1: 'The same run never teaches and validates.'
- V2.1 27.3 and 27.8: validation plans are structurally outside the learning corpus and use fresh sessions and fixtures, so a validation plan has no learning run. This applies to EV-V-FX-2F, EV-V-FX-4F and EV-V-FX-BIG, all under PARAM-02 in BA-04 V3.
- The 19 x (N_det + 1) term also adds the reference run to these 3 validation scenarios.

For validation, use either the first governing validation run of the plan (N_det + 1 runs) or the frozen EVM's f(plan) (N_det runs, no extra run). Adjust the expression accordingly.

findings.location: s2.1 PARAM-01 and EVIDENCE_REPETITION rows (lines 31, 36); s2.2 PARAM-01 strictest-pair and scope bullets (lines 47-49); s2.3 'EVIDENCE 37' (line 79)
findings.claim: The strictest-pair rule that BA10-02 and AR2-43 require is applied only to the DEFAULT, CHAR and CLEAN rules. Governing scenarios under other rules that serve class-A groups get fewer runs, and non-governing scenarios sit under a parameter defined as governing runs.
findings.evidence:
- BA-04 V3: EV-V-FX-2F, -4F and -BIG (VALIDATION, GOVERNING, rule LEARN = N_det+1) serve class-A groups (ID-A, E4, E6, E9, LK, PR-REC, PW, KS, SC-A, E8) as well as class-B groups.
- PR-CLOSURE-COMPLETENESS (group PR-REC, class A, GOVERNING) uses EVIDENCE_REPETITION, although line 36 limits that value to Q, U-*, S1, PP and CL. Those groups total 36 scenarios; BA-10's 'EVIDENCE 37' counts this one as well.
- CHAR includes E4-LEARN-R1-LM1/LM2 and LK-LM1/LM2-PROPS/CONFLICT (NON_GOVERNING_BY_DESIGN per AR2-11) and E6-C4 (EXPLORATORY_NON_GOVERNING). PARAM-01 is defined as 'governing runs per scenario', and no intent is stated for these. For the E-04 pin the intent would be the probability of missing an admitted-set member, which would then fail every governing R-1 run.
findings.required_fix: Apply max(N_strict, rule value) to every governing scenario that serves a class-A or class-B group, whatever its rule; or move PR-CLOSURE-COMPLETENESS to DEFAULT in BA-04. State the intent of the repetitions of the non-governing CHAR scenarios, or give them their own parameter, and correct the wording in 2.1.

findings.location: s4 heading and rows 2-3 (lines 104-110)
findings.claim: The new heading makes every row 'part of BASE-18'. That places the evidence-derived pins (the E-04 admitted set and LOCK_MODE) and the E-04 route under BASE-18.

findings.location: s1 second bullet (line 21); s2.1 PARAM-05 row (line 35) and s2.2 line 67; s5 intro (line 114) and Q-O5 (line 122)
findings.claim: The sheet is inconsistent about who may answer Q-O5, the machine-class policy.

rulings.item: Is BA-07 ready for CANDIDATE_FOR_SEALING while the independent copy is undesignated?
rulings.recommendation: No, not now. Under AR2-39 an undesignated copy is admissible only if the candidate ruling itself designates the location and the holder, and BA-07 says where that designation is recorded and that 6.2 step 6 reads it (BA07-V3-05). The candidate ruling also has to wait for BA07-V3-01, -02 and -03 to be fixed, and for BA-01 to reach CANDIDATE_FOR_SEALING (BA-11 V3 §2 requires every DEPENDS_ON entry to be at least a candidate).
rulings.reasoning: The simulation shows that an honest log fails at the first re-anchor after an IN_USE entry. Anchor discovery can be defeated by truncating the log tail without rewriting any remote reference. The custody of pins after the baseline contradicts BA-11. BA-07 is a procedure sealed at the baseline, so each of these would need a new version and a new anchor if fixed after sealing. BA-01 is still DRAFT because V2.4 revision 2 awaits the Coordinator's textual verification.

rulings.item: Who owns WU_DRY_RUNS (BA10-V3-04)?
rulings.recommendation: Derive it from Q-O2 (N_B), as BA-10 and BA-11 V3 do, and correct BA-09 V3 (lines 50 and 85) and BA-04 V3 (lines 91 and 429).
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 13.1 (line 732) makes the dry-run count a classified parameter of the class-B group WU. The phase-1 ruling reserves p and alpha to the Owner. The dry runs are the largest cost term. Letting the Coordinator pick the count directly would move an Owner-derived risk choice to the Coordinator.

rulings.item: What unit should MAX_ATTEMPTS (PARAM-04) use?
rulings.recommendation: Per planned governing run (per repetition slot). Every attempt of that slot counts, contamination included. A slot that exhausts m leaves the scenario without one of its required governing runs, so its group cannot be PASS.
rulings.reasoning: This keeps AR2-43 (a procedural cap with no host evidence) and V2.1 21.3 (scheduled repeats are not retries). It also avoids the contradiction between a per-scenario cap m >= 1 and N required governing runs (BA10-V3-02).

rulings.item: What is the membership of the PARAM-03 clean sample?
rulings.recommendation: Declare it explicitly and define K as its size. Include EA2-DEFERRED-EVENTS only if its writer-free runs are declared part of the false-rejection sample under V2.1 10.6. Write the rule symbolically in BA-10 and word AR2-28 the same way.
rulings.reasoning: As written, 'CL-CLEAN-* (9 scenarios)' matches neither the 8 CL-CLEAN-<fixture> scenarios nor the 9 scenarios under the CLEAN rule. In the regime ceil(n/9) > N_strict, the 8 CL-CLEAN-* scenarios deliver fewer than n runs (BA10-V3-01).

rulings.item: What do AR2-16's 'entrada en BA-11' and 'sello propio' mean for pins written after the baseline?
rulings.recommendation: The Architect should clarify. Suggested reading: BA-11 carries only sealed slot definitions and never receives a value. The pin's seal is a pair of Coordinator and Architect ratification records that cite the pin-record hash. BA-07 custodies those records with PIN_RECORDED and the anchor.
rulings.reasoning: Otherwise every pin write either forces a new BA-11 version and a new baseline anchor, or edits a sealed registry in place (BA07-V3-03).

rulings.item: PH2D-1 and the timing of the Owner memo
rulings.recommendation: Record the corrected total (9377, not 9358) and the other three corrected rows. Do not put Q-O1..Q-O5 to the Owner until BA10-V3-01, -04, -05 and -06 are corrected.
rulings.reasoning: The memo is the Owner's decision input. Its cost figures and sensitivities are currently wrong, and the scope of Q-O2 (whether it covers the dry runs) is contested between the V3 artifacts.

rulings.item: Does the PARAM-04 method need host evidence?
rulings.recommendation: No. It complies with AR2-43.
rulings.reasoning: Line 65 grounds the cap only in V2.1 21.3 (every INVALID retry needs authorization per occurrence) and in V2.1 1.3. The beta/observed-rate method was withdrawn. Any later revision informed by dry runs is a new baseline version.

candidate_readiness.reason:
Four reasons:
- It has three new MAJOR defects. The verification rejects honest logs: at the first re-anchor after an IN_USE entry, at a repeated IN_USE, and at a re-anchor that covers several pins (BA07-V3-01). Anchor discovery is not taken from the remote tags (BA07-V3-02). Pin custody after the baseline contradicts BA-11 and AR2-16 (BA07-V3-03).
- The undesignated independent copy is acceptable under AR2-39 only if the candidate ruling designates it and BA-07 binds that designation (BA07-V3-05).
- BA-11 V3 §2 requires BA-01 to be at least CANDIDATE_FOR_SEALING first, and BA-01 is still DRAFT.
- If the BA-05 dependency (BA07-V3-06) is registered rather than removed, BA-07 would also wait for BA-05's candidate, which needs the library census.

Every value is UNSET. BASE-18 needs the Owner's answers to Q-O1..Q-O5, the Coordinator's PARAM-04 and EVIDENCE_REPETITION, a host observation for the PARAM-05 label (not authorized), and the TOL_SCALE decision (K-3). The sealed bytes must carry these values, so candidacy can only follow those decisions. The method also has four MAJOR defects (BA10-V3-01..04), and the Owner memo is not yet accurate enough to be asked (BA10-V3-05, BA10-V3-06).
