findings.location: section 4, 'Sealed reason for SL-Y "added"' (line 98)
findings.claim: For a mirror of a product-drawn rack, no RackCad layer is added unless one was renamed or removed outside RackCad after the source was drawn ('evidence sa3a S5, S6 as corrected by its verifier').
findings.evidence: The claim assumes the mirror's labels follow the source's inputs, but the mirror's Name differs from the source's. sa3a S4 (CONFIRMED): a blank or whitespace Name suppresses the rack-name label even with DrawRackName on (SelectiveFrontalBuilder.cs:342, SelectivePlantaBuilder.cs:338). LHD:258-270 ensures RACKCAD_ANOTACIONES only for a non-blank label. sa3a S6 verifier: 'Point (b), about the name, stands as stated'. The I-52 authority names the mirror '<base> - espejo', which is never blank: V17 PDC-2 (proposal-v17.md:352), ID-4 (:1060), S-17 (:1768, 'anotaciones regeneradas con el nombre logico destino') and T-M26 (:3755). Blank-named Selective racks are product-reachable (RackSelectivoCommands.cs:459, 520; RackViewBaseName.cs:22-37 fallbacks; this is why AUTH-15-C1 was made). Consequence: a blank-named source with DrawRackName on, NumberFronts/NumberLevels off and no other RackCad annotation has no RACKCAD_ANOTACIONES, and its mirror must add it, with no rename or removal. BA-06 V3 section 10.2 repeats the unsound claim.
findings.required_fix: Rewrite the sealed reason to cover the blank-name case. Preferably add a fixture variant, for example FX-ANN-BLANK (Name blank, DrawRackName on, other toggles off, Dimensions None): it is product-reachable, keeps the source valid, needs no L-29/L-33 exception, and gives a governing clean scenario for SL-Y 'added' (the first alternative of BA08-01). At minimum, add the case to the disclosed residual. Correct the SH-LAY-ADDED wording in BA-06 V3 section 10.2.

findings.location: section 2, differences table, row 'envelope input' (line 43)
findings.claim: AUTH-15 overload A 'writes the caller's bytes verbatim', unlike the product path, which re-serializes.
findings.evidence: At 3375aadb, RackDefinitionCreator.CreateInTransaction takes 'RackEmbedDocument envelope' (RDC:45). Precheck serializes it itself: 'payloadJson = new RackEmbedStore().Serialize(envelope);' (RDC:187). Envelope() writes that string (RDC:204) and compares the read-back with it, not with caller bytes (RDC:206). Both paths therefore re-serialize a RackEmbedDocument; the product path does it at RackSelectivoCommands.cs:405-417. BA08-07's evidence already said so: 're-serializes it (RackDefinitionCreator.cs:187) instead of writing caller bytes'. As written, the row credits AUTH-15 with the mirror requirement C-127, which it does not meet, in the table the Architect uses for PH2-CF-1.
findings.required_fix: AUTH-15 cell: 'takes a RackEmbedDocument, re-serializes it with RackEmbedStore.Serialize (RDC:187), writes and reads back its own serialization (ordinal)'. Add that neither path meets C-127 (caller bytes verbatim; PA-8 unknown members) and that this is one reason no AUTH-15 evidence transfers.

findings.location: section 5, phase-A domain (line 102), versus section 4 row SL-Y (line 93)
findings.claim: Phase A adjudicates (1) SL-S, SL-P and the pre-existing containers of SL-C, and (2) the objects created in T_M. At PV the sealed PROTECTED_OBJECTS is checked for consistency with that domain.
findings.evidence: V2.1 10.3: PROTECTED_OBJECTS include every element of the sealed list. So both reuse clean scenarios, whose expected result in BA-04 V3 is 'every control PASS', would abort at PV. Events on the reused layer during T_M would also go unadjudicated in phase A.

findings.location: section 4, WARMUP_COVERAGE_CRITERION (line 50)

In those runs E-11M is evaluated fail-closed (V2.1 3.2), and U-5 is itself a canary-load scenario. V2.1 13.1 defines the criterion per scenario, with no exception for evidence groups. findings.location: section 11 rule 5 (line 179); section 16.2 K-4 (line 242)
findings.claim: HOST_DEFAULT_MAP is a pin 'derived from non-governing characterization'.
findings.evidence: No V3 artifact defines that characterization. The BA-04 V3 JSON has no scenario that produces it, although 137 governing scenarios carry the HOST_DEFAULT_MAP slot. BA-11 V3 section 3.1 gives the source only as 'non-governing characterization'. Every other pin has a named source: E04 from E4-LEARN-R1-*, LOCK_MODE from LK-*, EVM from learning. BA-06 V3 section 5 treats host defaults only as a residual that surfaces as events. V17 L-36 (proposal-v17.md:421) assigns this characterization to CT-50, with a MaterializationContextReadSet: CLAYER, CECOLOR, CELTYPE, CELTSCALE, CELWEIGHT, CETRANSPARENCY, CPLOTSTYLE, and the dimension-style and text-style records. Without a defined derivation, 'never derived from governing outputs' cannot be audited and K-4 cannot be discharged.
findings.required_fix: Define the derivation as named NON_GOVERNING_BY_DESIGN scenarios in BA-04: their fixtures, which context variables are varied, and what is recorded. Key the map by the consumed context variables, reconcile it with V17 L-36/CT-50, and name those scenarios as the pin source in BA-11.

findings.location: section 4 row SL-R (line 90); section 11 rule 1 (line 175) and rule 5 (line 179)
findings.claim: SL-R compares name, position, scale, rotation, normal and layer. Rule 1 takes only the layer from the I-52 authority. Rule 5 sends colour, linetype and lineweight to HOST_DEFAULT_MAP 'where the I-52 authority gives none'.
findings.evidence: V17 ST-13 (proposal-v17.md:918) requires the new reference to keep, explicitly assigned, the LayerId, Color, Linetype, LinetypeScale, LineWeight, Transparency and Visible of its source reference (and PlotStyleName under STB). The I-52 authority therefore does give these values, so rule 5 excludes them, and no rule derives them. Rule 1 cites L-33 ('keeps the presentation of the source') but reads only the layer.
findings.required_fix: Cite ST-13. Extend SL-R and rule 1 to the full ST-13 set, read from the source reference into the PRE_COMMAND_STATE_RECORD, and restrict rule 5 to nested references, DBText and dimensions.

findings.location: section 7, catalog hashes and 'Rule' (line 134); section 3, 'Tuple consequence' (line 67)
findings.claim: The universe is 're-derived from, or asserted equal to, the catalog files pinned in the tuple', and the listed hashes are blob SHA-256.
findings.evidence: The comment in .gitattributes at 3375aadb says the repository works with core.autocrlf=true. blocks.csv, secciones.csv and the other name-determining catalogs are not marked -text, so the deployed runtime copies have CRLF line endings and will not hash to the listed LF blob values (sa3b limitation). Two further gaps: (a) the provider reads every *.csv and *.json in the directory (signature, JsonRackCatalogProvider.cs:220-247), not only the 7 listed files; (b) CatalogDirectory.Resolve falls back to AppContext.BaseDirectory.
findings.required_fix: State that the comparison is of the derived name universe, or pin the deployed bytes separately from the blob hashes. Define the tuple field as the resolved directory path plus every *.csv/*.json in it.

findings.location: section 6.1 (line 121); section 16.3 K-9 (line 249)
findings.claim: 'A static guard (EXEC-12) will assert that the seams and the warm-up harness do not reference those types'.
findings.evidence: The rule forbids the calls in 'the mirror's PREPARE-R and the warm-up'. The guard covers only 'the seams and the warm-up harness', not the orchestrator or PREPARE-R code. V2.1 23 defines EXEC-12 as the P-5 guards only (no Commit, Abort, Dispose, LockDocument, OpenCloseTransaction or side-database write; ReadBlockName removed), so this guard adds content to a contract item.
findings.required_fix: Extend the guard scope to the orchestrator and PREPARE-R. Register it as an additional execution prerequisite derived from AR2-42, not as EXEC-12.

findings.location: section 12, paragraph 'FX-IMP (K-8, AR2-41)' (line 209)
findings.claim: Example of a reachable construction: 'a source drawn in a drawing whose library later lacks a block that the mirror needs'.
findings.evidence: A library that later lacks a block does not remove the block from the drawing: the source's nested definitions still reference it. If the drawing also lacked it, the import would fail (a MissingLibraryBlocks refusal), not follow the import path. The reachable construction is the reverse: the source is drawn while the library lacks the blocks, the pieces are omitted and reported (sa3b F1.1-F1.5), and the library later supplies them.
findings.required_fix: Replace the example, or remove it and leave the construction to K-8.

findings.location: section 10, TOL_CONTINUITY paragraph (line 165)
findings.claim: 'No Selective quantity is classed "computed by normalization"'.
findings.evidence: V17 4.3 (proposal-v17.md:968) and :2643 give Continuity (1e-7) to values written by a declared normalization, N-S02, which is the Selective medio frente. The conclusion is still correct for CT-21D: the comparison is writer output against the sealed plan capture, N-S02 is part of mu_k correctness (rule 4), and the fixtures have no medio frente.
findings.required_fix: Reword: in CT-21D comparisons no quantity is computed by normalization, because N-S02 (V17 4.3) is outside CT-21D and the fixtures exclude medio frente.

findings.location: section 11, Inputs (line 171)
findings.claim: A 'deep, canonical, hashed capture' of each plan is sealed in PREPARE-R.
findings.evidence: No V3 artifact defines the canonical serialization, record type or digest of the plan capture. BA-05 V3 has no plan-capture record, so the sealed hash is not reproducible by a second party.
findings.required_fix: Define the capture as a record type (for example in BA-05 V3): fields, order, number encoding and digest. Log its digest in PREPARE-R.

findings.location: section 11 rule 2 (line 176)
findings.claim: The expected dynamic-property set is the plan's parameters intersected with the writable properties the block exposes, and the expected values are the plan values.
findings.evidence: LHD:432-436 assigns property.Value. A dynamic parameter with a value set (list or increment) can store a value other than the one assigned. The BA-05 V3 census record keeps only dynamicProperties (name, writable) (BA-05 V3 line 894), so neither the census nor the oracle can predict a constrained value.
findings.required_fix: Add value-set constraints to the census record. Either make the expected value the constrained value, or declare constrained properties UNKNOWN until they are characterized.

findings.location: section 3, row 'entity types' (line 57)
findings.claim: 'negative scale only on nested piece references'.
findings.evidence: LHD:62 gives an X-mirror scale to nested-group placement references in the view definition. LHD:313 sets MirroredX/MirroredY scale on every piece reference, loose (view definition) or nested (sa2 F05-S03). Only the top-level reference never has a negative scale.
findings.required_fix: Reword: negative scale can appear on any reference inside the view definition (piece or group placement), never on the top-level reference.

findings.location: section 3, row 'E-12 handler code' (line 44)
findings.claim: The E-12 handler code is 'attached to the side database only; detached before step 4'.
findings.evidence: V2.1 14.1 E-12 STRUCTURE_CLASS consists of document-collection, document-command and editor events. These cannot be attached to a side database, which is the same objection BA09-04 raised for E-11M. Only WRITE_CLASS and TX_CLASS can be scoped to the side database.
findings.required_fix: Warm the STRUCTURE_CLASS handlers the same way as E-11M (direct invocation, not subscribed), or declare them as residual. Keep this consistent with PA-12 ('no event generated in the governed logs').

findings.location: section 6 (lines 58-74); section 3, E-11M row (line 45)
findings.claim: The static-state enumeration lists the RackCad product statics, and the E-11M handler is invoked directly 'so no event reaches the governed E-11M log'.
findings.evidence: PA-5(11) covers any retained state that could alter the window, including control-plane instrument state the warm-up exercises: I-01 sequence counters, I-15 writers, and the E-11M and E-12 handlers' sink and sequence. V2.1 13.2 and 14.2 treat a sequence gap as UNKNOWN. The text does not say which sink the directly invoked handler writes to, or that counters and buffers start fresh at step 4. Rows 6 and 8 also leave out the Application and Domain tier-B singletons (SystemRegistry.Default and others; sa4 limitations).
findings.required_fix: Require warm-up-only instrument instances or sinks, and state that no counter or buffer carries into the governed logs; WU-BOUNDARY should check that the governed logs start at the initial sequence number. Add a row for the Application and Domain tier-B statics.

findings.location: section 3, row SL-1/SL-2 (line 39)
findings.claim: The row exercises 'piece references, dynamic parameters' and says 'its effects stay in the side database (evidence sa4 CORE-15)'.
findings.evidence: The CORE-15 verifier limits that statement to repository statics. Whether AdjustAlignment (LHD:280), RecomputeDimensionBlock (:375) and dynamic-block evaluation (:432-447) leave host-internal state is runtime behaviour. sa4 'missed' item 3: on a fresh side database, CreateSystemBlock skips every piece (LHD:293-303), so piece references and ApplyDynamicParameters run only if the SL-5 import into that side database happens first. The artifact does not state that order.
findings.required_fix: Restrict the claim to repository statics and assign host-internal effects to WARMUP_STATIC_STATE_RESIDUAL. State that the SL-5 import into the side database precedes SL-1 and SL-2 in step 1.

findings.location: section 6, row UserSettingsStore (line 67)
findings.claim: The treatment is 'file-system side effect only; the control plane records the hash of settings.json before and after'.
findings.evidence: Quarantining a corrupt settings.json (sa4 CORE-14) changes how the governed window resolves the library path (BlockLibraryLocator.ResolvePath reads settings on every call: override lost, default path used), so it can alter the window. The row records the hash but says nothing about what a change means.
findings.required_fix: Either forbid the warm-up from calling UserSettingsStore, or state that a changed settings.json hash refuses the run (O1) or makes it INVALID.

findings.location: section 4 (line 50); section 8, W-2 (line 85)
findings.claim: WU_DRY_RUNS is 'the Coordinator value'.
findings.evidence: BA-10 V3 PARAM-01 (lines 30 and 48) sets WU_DRY_RUNS = N_B, computed from Owner-reserved p_B and alpha_B (Q-O2). The Coordinator only records the value.
findings.required_fix: Reword: 'WU_DRY_RUNS = N_B of PARAM-01 (Owner choice of p_B, alpha_B; recorded by the Coordinator)'.

rulings.item: WU-Q1 row 1: JsonRackCatalogProvider.Cache, entry under a warm-up-only directory key
rulings.recommendation: NOT COMPATIBLE as proposed. Preferred: drop the Load() on a catalog copy. If the per-scenario WU-DRY runs show an assembly load on the first governed catalog read, warm only the type initializer (an empty Cache, the same state the window itself would create) and the dependent assemblies, adding no entry. Keep the entry only through a recorded Architect interpretation or amendment of PA-5(11) with conditions: a key disjoint under OrdinalIgnoreCase; a harness observation of the Cache key set at step 3 and at CP; and a static guard that no mirror-path code builds a provider on a non-governed directory.
rulings.reasoning: PA-5(11) prohibits 'any other retained state' besides the loaded code, and the parenthetical reads categorically. The entry, holding a parsed RackCatalog, stays for the whole process: src has no Remove or Clear, and GetOrAdd inserts the entry even if the load throws (sa4 CORE-09). The implementer's reading ('the window never reads it') relies only on the first clause. The phase-2 fix alternative required a control-plane observation proving no effect, and V3 declares 'none without reflection'. The governed key does stay untouched: the key is the raw directory string, the Selective planta builder receives the catalog it is passed (SelectivePlantaBuilder.cs:45), and PluginInitializer is empty. So the risk is small, but the text does not allow it without a ruling.

rulings.item: WU-Q1 row 2: BlockLibraryDatabaseCache
rulings.recommendation: COMPATIBLE (not touched), provided the static guard also covers the orchestrator and PREPARE-R (D-09).
rulings.reasoning: The warm-up uses its own copy and Database and never calls Acquire (BA-08 section 6.1), so the single slot stays empty and no state is left. A call would evict or replace the slot (sa4 CORE-02), so the no-call rule must be enforced wherever it applies.

rulings.item: WU-Q1 row 3: RackLog.sink
rulings.recommendation: COMPATIBLE. Keep the record of the log directory's file list and sizes.
rulings.reasoning: In production the sink keeps its initializer value (RackLog.cs:18). RedirectForTests is internal and InternalsVisibleTo grants only the test project, so no static state changes. Appending to the log is a file effect and does not change behaviour inside the window.

rulings.item: WU-Q1 row 4: UserSettingsStore
rulings.recommendation: COMPATIBLE with PA-5(11), but the boundary treatment is incomplete (D-18).
rulings.reasoning: There is no static state. A quarantined settings.json does change the governed window's library-path resolution, so detection without a stated consequence, or without forbidding the call, does not protect the window.

rulings.item: WU-Q1 row 5: CsvStructuralSectionCatalogProvider.Cache
rulings.recommendation: COMPATIBLE (not reached).
rulings.reasoning: It is reached only through the structural-section and Cantilever paths (sa4 CORE-12), which the Selective warm-up does not call.

rulings.item: WU-Q1 row 6: RackFrameTemplateCatalog.All
rulings.recommendation: COMPATIBLE as a consequence of executing the loaded code.
rulings.reasoning: The warm-up leaves this static exactly as the window would: type initialization of a constant, input-independent built-in list (RackFrameTemplateCatalog.cs:21), never written afterwards (sa3b F8.5). The tier-B classification rests on grep; that limitation is declared.

rulings.item: WU-Q1 row 7: static JsonSerializerOptions and the framework metadata caches
rulings.recommendation: PARTIALLY COMPATIBLE. The repository options objects (tier B) are acceptable as executed code. The framework per-type metadata caches and the locking of the options must be classed as WARMUP_STATIC_STATE_RESIDUAL (disclosed), not as 'code loaded'.
rulings.reasoning: CORE-19 is UNCERTAIN: this is framework behaviour. BA-09's own residual paragraph already lists 'framework and host caches'. Classing the caches as loaded code contradicts that paragraph, and the residual clause of PA-5 is where they belong.

rulings.item: WU-Q1 row 8: other Plugin statics (KindHandlerRegistry.Default and others)
rulings.recommendation: COMPATIBLE. Extend the row to the tier-B statics of Application and Domain (D-16).
rulings.reasoning: These statics are only initialized, never written afterwards (sa4 CORE-21). Initialization is part of executing the loaded code.

rulings.item: WU-Q1 row 9: the four tier-A statics of RackCad.UI
rulings.recommendation: COMPATIBLE (not reached). Keep E-11M and E-10 detection of a RackCad.UI load.
rulings.reasoning: The mirror and harness paths open no window, so UI code does not run and its statics stay untouched.

rulings.item: PH2-CF-1 (AUTH-15 fact)
rulings.recommendation: ACCEPT as a correction of fact only: no change to the 15.3 design clauses, no transfer of evidence, P-8 still required, AR2-38 applies. Record the correction of F-2 in V2.1 15.1 through an errata or the decisions log (a baseline artifact cannot amend the contract). Correct the differences table first (D-02).
rulings.reasoning: I verified the fact. Overload A takes any HeaderRunPlan (RDC:39-45). SelectiveFrontalBuilder.BuildPlan and SelectivePlantaBuilder.BuildPlan return HeaderRunPlan. RackDefinitionCreator has no production caller. F-2's 'frontal and planta have no caller-owned seam' is therefore incomplete. AUTH-15 still differs from the SL-1/SL-2 contract: it re-serializes the envelope, detects missing blocks after writing, and checks the transaction via TopTransaction.UnmanagedObject.

rulings.item: PH2-TP-1 (catalog folder in the tuple)
rulings.recommendation: ACCEPT in substance, as a BUILD_BOUND tuple field. Adding the field changes V2.1 2.1, so it needs a contract-level instrument: a pre-approved micro-errata or an Architect ruling verified by the Coordinator.

rulings.item: PH2-OR-1 (HOST_DEFAULT_MAP as a pin)
rulings.reasoning: The drawers leave these attributes unset (LHD:266-277, 308-314; BP:182), so neither the plan nor the code can give expected values. V17 L-36 names the host's effective values as a characterization item. A pin from non-governing evidence keeps the oracle independent of the writer and of governing outputs. It is not a tolerance, so PA-9 does not apply.

rulings.item: PH2-E4-1 (R-1 delivery by keystrokes)
rulings.reasoning: Phase 2 refuted BA08-06 2 of 2: the control plane is excluded from 'any other process'. R-3 (.scr) is excluded by the phase-1 ruling item 12 and by V2.1 3.3. BA-08 section 8 and BA-04 Q-ROUTE-R1 already keep route identity (recorded) separate from the CMDACTIVE bits (observations).

rulings.item: Sealed reason for SL-Y 'added' (BA-08 V3 section 4)
rulings.recommendation: NOT ACCEPTABLE (D-01).
rulings.reasoning: The cited evidence contradicts it: sa3a S6 point (b) was upheld by the verifier, and V17 PDC-2/ID-4/S-17/T-M26 give the mirror the name '<base> - espejo', which is never blank. A blank-named source with DrawRackName on and no other annotation reaches 'added' with no rename or removal. That case gives a product-reachable, L-29/L-33-clean fixture for a governing SL-Y 'added' scenario, which is the first alternative of BA08-01. The rename case can stay a disclosed residual.

findings.artifact: docs/initiatives/I-52-ct21d-baseline-ba-11-hash-registry-v3.md (section 2.1, line 51; row BA-05 line 64; BASE-14 line 131) with docs/initiatives/I-52-ct21d-baseline-ba-05-fingerprint-specification-v3.md (section 3.3 SV-06/SV-07/SV-10/SV-11, lines 863-868; section 5, lines 885-887; section 6 L-2, line 903) and docs/automation/evidence/I-52-ct21d-fpspec-v1-vectors-v3.gen.py (lines 504-515)
findings.location: BA-11 V3 section 2.1 claim that the V2 cycle BA-05 <-> BA-08 is broken; BA-05 V3 sections 3.3, 5 and 6
findings.claim: The BA-05 <-> BA-08 cycle that BA11-F3 required to be broken still exists in content. BA-05's NORMATIVE semantic vectors hardcode BA-08 tolerance values, and BA-05's census procedure takes its universe from BA-08. So BA-11's statements 'BA-08 depends on BA-05 ..., not the reverse' and 'the graph is acyclic' are false under BA-11's own definition of a dependency.
findings.evidence: AR2-35 says the tolerance values live ONLY in BA-08 and BA-05 names the slots. But BA-05 V3 section 3.3, 'NORMATIVE semantic comparison vectors', gives these rules, generated verbatim by gen.py lines 504-515: SV-06 '5e-10 <= TOL_LENGTH = 1e-9 in'; SV-07 '2e-9 > TOL_LENGTH'; SV-10 '5e-10 <= TOL_ANGLE = 1e-9 rad'; SV-11 'atan(2e-9) > TOL_NORMAL = 1e-9 rad'. Their EQUAL/DIFFERENT results depend on BA-08 V3 section 10 lines 159-160 (TOL_LENGTH 1e-9 in; TOL_ANGLE, TOL_NORMAL 1e-9 rad). BA-05 section 5 step 1 enumerates 'every block definition of the static universe of BA-08 V3 section 7 (46 names)', and step 2 uses 'BA-08 V3 section 11 rule 2'. The census types must enter BA-05 before its candidate (BA-11 row BA-05, line 64). BA-08 in turn depends on BA-05 section 5 and on the census (K-2). BA-05 section 6 L-2 keeps NB-3 open on BA-08's K-3, which BA-11's BASE-14 row (line 131, 'census pending') leaves out. BA-11 section 2.1 defines 'X depends on Y when a normative value of X is defined in Y' and seals BA-05 in tier 1, before BA-08. So a later BA-08 version that changes a tolerance or the section 7 universe would not cascade to a sealed BA-05.
findings.required_fix: Remove the BA-05 -> BA-08 content edges. Either (a) make SV-06/07/10/11 parametric: declare explicit vector-local test tolerances inside BA-05, labelled as vector parameters and not the kind values, or move those vectors to BA-08. And define the census universe without reference to BA-08, for example every block definition of the library file (a superset), or make the census record its own registry item that is ordered after BA-08 section 7 and that both artifacts depend on. Or (b) record the edges and fix the seal order and cascade to match. Then correct the BA-11 section 2.1 rationale and add TOL_SCALE (NB-3 L-2) to the BASE-14 row.

findings.location: section 2.1 (line 51) and seal order (line 54); DEPENDS_ON cells of rows BA-06 (line 65), BA-07 (line 66), BA-10 (line 67), BA-04 (line 70)

Row BA-04 omits BA-09, and line 54 puts 'BA-09, BA-04' in the same tier, even though the WU-Q1 ruling on BA-09 section 6 is still open. (2) BA-07 -> BA-05: BA-07 V3 line 61 (canonical serialization) says 'doubles as in BA-05 V3 section 2.1'. (3) BA-10 -> BA-07: the PARAM-05 label at BA-10 V3 line 73 uses 'the canonical serialization (BA-07 V3 section 4)'. (4) BA-06 -> BA-03: the q2 domain at BA-06 V3 line 689 is taken from 'the scope row SEL-PLANTA of BA-03 V3'. (5) BA-10 -> BA-04, which makes a cycle because BA-04 -> BA-10 is listed. The normative PARAM-03 combination rule at BA-10 V3 line 61, section 2.2, hardcodes the BA-04 count: 'max(N_strict, ceil(n / 9))' with '9 scenarios in BA-04 V3'. BA-04's own REPETITION_RULES.CLEAN is symbolic ('number of CL-CLEAN scenarios') and cites BA-10. BA-11 line 51 exempts only the counts of 'BA-10 section 2.3', but this constant is in section 2.2. Rows BA-06, BA-07 and BA-10 list only BA-01 plus external inputs.

Either add the edges BA-07 -> BA-05, BA-10 -> BA-07 and BA-06 -> BA-03 and order tier 1 to match, or state in 2.1 why each one is only a mention. Make the BA-10 PARAM-03 rule symbolic (|CL-CLEAN| of the sealed catalog), as in AR2-28 and BA-04, and mark the 9 as informative. Then re-check that the graph is acyclic and publish the full edge list.

findings.location: section 3.1 (lines 74-86); rule 4 (line 45); row BA-11 DEPENDS_ON 'every other entry' (line 72); BA-07 V3 line 21 item (b), lines 119-120, line 162
findings.claim: The pin records are 'entries' of the registry, but they are written after the baseline. Under BA-11's own rules this means either a deadlock or an undefined re-versioning of the sealed registry on every pin.
findings.evidence: Section 3.1 says a pin value 'lives in a pin record with its own entry below, its own seal and its custody entries', with STATUS and PIN_RECORD_HASH columns in BA-11. Rule 4 seals the final registry 'after every other entry is SEALED', and the BA-11 row depends on 'every other entry'. Pins are written 'after the baseline and before the first governing run' (BA-07 V3 line 21(b); BA-04 V3 section 2.1). Their sources, E4-LEARN, LK-*, EVM learning and fixture instances, are all execution-phase host work. Read literally, BA-11 can never be sealed. The alternative reading also fails. Writing a pin into BA-11 after its seal is 'a new registry version with a new anchor' (rule 4). That changes the BA-11 seal hash, which is the BASELINE subjectHash of the genesis entry (BA-07 section 8), and so supersedes the BASELINE (BA-07 line 119). This contradicts BA-07 step 7 (line 162), which re-anchors pins as custody events of the same baseline ('<version>-a<n>'), and the SEALED_PENDING_PIN design. AR2-16 asks for an 'entrada en BA-11' but does not say how it interacts with the seal.
findings.required_fix: State that 'every other entry' in rule 4 and in the BA-11 row means the artifact entries of section 3 only. Declare section 3.1 a slot table sealed with BA-11 (slots and the rule for where values are recorded). After the baseline, pin values, STATUS and PIN_RECORD_HASH are authoritative only in the pin records and the custody log (PIN_RECORDED/ANCHORED) and are never written into BA-11, in parallel with rule 2. Otherwise define explicitly a registry re-version per pin that is not a new baseline version, and align the BA-07 BASELINE state machine with it. This needs an Architect ruling that refines AR2-16.

findings.location: BA-04 JSON field SEALED_AT (370 scenarios, all 'UNSET'); BA-04 md section 7 C-8 (line 434) and section 2 (lines 41-46); BA-11 V3 rule 1 (line 42)
findings.claim: This is the residual of BA11-F2. The catalog keeps an in-file hash field per scenario (SEALED_AT), and no rule says when or where it is recorded. BA-04 also talks of per-scenario sealing, which the registry does not model.
findings.evidence: V2.1 26.1 (line 1393) defines SEALED_AT as 'the hash of the expectation, recorded before the first governing run of the scenario'. BA-04 C-8 says 'then the seal (SEALED_AT) scenario by scenario', and the SEALED_CANDIDATE status means 'ready for the candidate ruling'. BA-11 has one artifact-level entry for BA-04 with one SEAL_HASH. The STATUS_AUTHORITY clause covers the per-scenario 'statuses', not SEALED_AT. Writing SEALED_AT after the Architect's candidate ruling would change the catalog bytes and expire the candidate (BA-11 line 36). Rule 1's parenthesis says the V3 artifacts no longer carry seal-hash fields.
findings.required_fix: State in BA-11 (and BA-04) that each SEALED_AT is computed from the scenario's expectation fields and written before the BA-04 candidate ruling, so it is covered by the candidate hash. Otherwise, derive it and record it only in the BA-04 ratification or seal records, with the in-file value declared frozen. Reword C-8 and SEALED_CANDIDATE so that sealing is at artifact level.

findings.location: section 2, row 'cascade' (line 37)
findings.claim: The cascade rule does not cover a dependency that is RATIFIED, and it does not say that the dependents' ratifications also expire.
findings.evidence: The rule covers 'a new version of an entry that is CANDIDATE_FOR_SEALING or SEALED'. RATIFIED is a separate state (line 28). A dependent can become a candidate when its dependency is 'at least CANDIDATE_FOR_SEALING' (line 33), which includes RATIFIED. A RATIFIED dependency that is re-versioned would therefore not expire its dependents' candidates. The row names 'candidates and seals' only, not ratifications.
findings.required_fix: Reword the rule as 'an entry that is at least CANDIDATE_FOR_SEALING (CANDIDATE_FOR_SEALING, RATIFIED or SEALED)', and say that the dependents' candidates, ratifications and seals expire.

findings.location: section 2 transitions (lines 33, 35) versus DEPENDS_ON cells of rows BA-05, BA-06, BA-10, BA-08, BA-09 (lines 64-69)
findings.claim: The normative DEPENDS_ON column mixes registry entries with prerequisites that are not artifacts. The transition rules then require registry states that those prerequisites cannot have.
findings.evidence: The cells include 'library census (host)', 'the evidence files bound inside it', 'Owner decisions Q-O1..Q-O5', 'Coordinator values PARAM-04 and EVIDENCE_REPETITION', 'the machine-attribute observation', 'TOL_SCALE decision, test and record (K-3)', 'FX-IMP construction (K-8)' and 'the Architect ruling WU-Q1'. Lines 33 and 35 require every DEPENDS_ON entry to be 'at least CANDIDATE_FOR_SEALING' or 'SEALED' with its SEAL_HASH cited. None of these items has such a state. Section 2.1 defines DEPENDS_ON as dependencies between artifacts.
findings.required_fix: Split the column into DEPENDS_ON, holding registry entries only and governed by the gating and cascade rules, and PREREQUISITES, holding external inputs. For each prerequisite, state the gate at which it must be met (before the candidate or before the seal) and its record.

findings.location: row BA-11 STATUS cell (line 72); rules 1-2 (lines 42-43)
findings.claim: The sole status authority gives BA-11's own status as a permanently frozen 'DRAFT', and no rule says where BA-11's status lives.
findings.evidence: Rule 1 makes the registry the only authority for 'the status and the hashes of every artifact'. Rule 2 moves BA-11's CANDIDATE_HASH, ratifications and SEAL_HASH outside, but not its STATUS. V2.1 8 and 14 say an unattributable event aborts before Commit(). With no EVM, no event on an object created inside T_M can be attributed, so the run aborts at PV. It then gets O2 by 17.2 row 3 and never reaches V0, V1 or PC.

**(3) PA-2 does not rescue the scenarios under either reading.**
- PA-2 governs the E12-V group verdict ('NOT_EVALUATED'), not the in-run fail-closed rule.

No control is declared to FAIL at PV unconditionally. Under the catalog default UNLISTED_CONTROLS (AR2-25), every other evaluated control, E-06 included, is expected PASS.

The sibling Y scenarios differ. NC-S1-Y1 and NC-E08-Y2 declare 'S1/E08 FAIL at PV' and 'abort before Commit is unconditional'. BA-04 V3 md 6.1 (G-1) states that 'The injected write uses T_M ... The target-control result and the abort are unconditional', which is AR2-18 ('el control objetivo y el abort, incondicionales'). NC-S5-O6 is a Y1 injection that uses neither T_M nor an unconditional abort.

(2) Phase-A domain. V2.2 PA-10 defines the domain as the protected objects determinable from the plan (source objects, relevant containers, NOD entries consumed) plus objects created inside T_M; outside it events are 'recorded, not adjudicated'. BA-08 V3 section 5 makes this concrete as SL-S, SL-P, the pre-existing containers of SL-C (block table names, model-space handles, sibling set, extension dictionaries) and the handles created in T_M. A pre-existing layer record is none of these. The E-08 read-set is also only the source authoritative read plus the consumed project variables (ALT-21D proposal V2 E-08; AR2-14; BA-08 V3 section 4 SL-S/SL-P), so it does not contain the layer.

FX-1F (BA-08 V3 section 12) has all toggles off and dimensions None, so no RackCad layer is an SL-Y element that S-1 compares. The layer is in the ABORT-VERIFY symbol-record read-set (BA-08 V3 section 6), but ABORT-VERIFY runs only after an abort. The conditional 'E12A FAIL' therefore contradicts PA-10, and nothing is designed to abort. If nothing aborts, the run commits (V2.1 17.2 rows 5-8) and O6 cannot occur. CER-PERSIST ('I-14 independent post-abort read') then has nothing to resolve, which makes the result UNKNOWN under md section 3.

I checked the claim against the V3 files at 1625a306 and the governing texts, and could not refute it.

1. **What the scenario expects.** BA-04 V3 JSON, NC-S5-O6 (lines 7033-7134):
   - PLAN_OR_INPUT says a pre-existing layer "of the PRE_COMMAND_STATE_RECORD" is changed through an OpenCloseTransaction at Y1. It then says "the change emits a phase-A event and the run aborts before Commit()". The layer is not named.
   - INJECTIONS lists only Wr-OCT. No harness-forced abort is declared, unlike AB-AFTER-MUTATION, which uses a canary load.
   - EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS lists only S5 (conditional) and E12A ("CONDITIONAL (CER-WIT): FAIL when the witness records the event delivered").
   - CONTROLS_EXERCISED also includes E06, S1, E08, E10 and E11M. Under DEFAULTS.UNLISTED_CONTROLS (AR2-25) all of these are expected PASS.
   - So by the catalog's own expectations, the only possible abort trigger is E12A, and that trigger is conditional. If the witness records no delivery, every expected result is PASS, nothing aborts, and the run commits. This contradicts the scenario's own PLAN.

2. **The object is outside the phase-A domain.**
   - V2.2 PA-10 defines the domain as the protected objects determinable from the plan (source objects, relevant containers, consumed NOD entries) plus objects created inside T_M. Events outside it are "recorded, not adjudicated".
   - BA-08 V3 section 5 makes this concrete: SL-S, SL-P, the pre-existing containers of SL-C, and the seam-created handles.
   - SL-C (section 4) lists block table names, model-space handles, the sibling set and extension dictionaries. No layer record is listed.
   - FX-1F (section 12) has all toggles off and dimensions `None`, so SL-Y is empty.
   - A pre-existing layer record is therefore outside the domain. E12A cannot FAIL on it even when the event is delivered.
   - If the layer were instead read as part of SL-S, E-08 would FAIL at PV. The catalog expects E08 PASS by default. Either reading leaves the scenario inconsistent.
   - By contrast, the catalog's own NC-E12A (AR2-25) deliberately targets "an object created inside T_M" so that E-12 phase A adjudicates it.

3. **It contradicts AR2-18 and the catalog's own rule.** AR2-18 says the target control and the abort are unconditional for non-silent Y injections. BA-04 V3 md section 6.1, line 389, restates this: "The target-control result and the abort are unconditional". NC-S5-O6 is a Y1 injection whose abort is conditional.

4. **The outcome cannot resolve if nothing aborts.**
   - ABORT-VERIFY runs only after Abort or FAILED (V2.1 section 11). A committed run follows 17.2 rows 5-8.
   - CER-PERSIST relies on a "post-abort read", which would not exist.
   - md section 3 says a rule that the sealed evidence cannot resolve makes the result UNKNOWN. A governing UNKNOWN is never retried and counts fail-closed for the group.

5. **E-06 PASS rests on an open question.** E06 is exercised and defaults to PASS. E6-C4 is EXPLORATORY_NON_GOVERNING with the value NOT_DECLARED. V2.1 4.2 declares OpenCloseTransaction visibility a blind spot. The expected E-06 result therefore depends on an uncharacterized question.

6. **CER-PERSIST is not registered.**
   - md section 3 "The declared rules" lists only CER-ABV, CER-WIT, CER-SIL and CER-A2.
   - The JSON CONDITIONAL_EXPECTATION_RULES has only CER-ABV, CER-WIT and CER-SIL.
   - The schema (md section 1) requires CONDITIONAL_EXPECTATION_RULE to be "a declared rule of section 3, or NONE".

7. **It is the only S-5 violation scenario.** BA-02b V3 line 32 lists NC-S5-O6 as the only S-5 violation scenario. That same row says S-5 needs "an induced failure of another control", which this scenario does not guarantee. V2.1 section 31, check 2, requires a deliberate-violation scenario per mandatory control, or a recorded reason that the control cannot be violated. This supports the required fix's fallback.

**Severity.** MAJOR is correct. The scenario is DRAFT and blocked by K-3, so this is not BLOCKING. But the group's only S-5 negative control cannot reliably produce its declared outcome and can end in a governing UNKNOWN.

The same sheet says a scenario "runs N governing times" (line 40) and that "N counts planned governing runs, not attempts" (line 50). The CLEAN rule adds max(N_strict, ceil(n/9)) runs (line 61) and LEARN adds N_det + 1 (line 53). So one scenario needs several governing runs.

(2) Attempts include governing runs. V2.1 21.3 (line 1117) keeps a per-scenario attempt log. It numbers every attempt and records each one's governing, non-governing or invalid state, and "every governing attempt counts". So the "attempts of a scenario" include its planned governing runs. Read literally, m is a per-scenario cap on all attempts. The only constraint stated is m >= 1. Any m below the required number of governing runs therefore makes the scenario impossible to complete. Nothing in BA-10 V3 relates m to N, n or N_det.

(3) No other artifact fixes the unit. BA-04 V3 s4 only sets RETRY_APPLICABILITY = NONE_AUTHORIZED, and its JSON has no attempt field. BA-11 V3 (BASE-9 and BASE-18 rows) and V2.2/2.3/2.4 do not define the unit either.

(4) AR2-43 does not settle it. It says "tope procedimental del Coordinador independiente de evidencia de host ... todo intento cuenta, incluida la contaminación". That governs the method change but says nothing about the unit. Following AR2-43 therefore does not remove the ambiguity. The withdrawn V2 method, "m consecutive attempts all INVALID", was naturally scoped to one slot. V3 dropped it without stating a replacement unit.

(5) The consequence rule is incomplete. Clause (4) covers only a scenario that reaches m "without a governing run", giving INVALID ("there is no governing run", V2.1 1.3). It says nothing about a scenario that hits the cap with 1 <= k < required governing runs. INVALID does not fit that case literally, because a governing run exists. PASS cannot apply either, because V2.1 1.3 requires every required governing run and 1.6 requires every required group to have a governing PASS. V2.1 1.6 would give NOT_EVALUATED at the predicate level, but the sheet states no group verdict for this case.

Severity. MAX_ATTEMPTS is MUST_FIX_BEFORE_AUTHORITY_BASELINE (V2.1 21.7, BASE-18). The method sealed here is what the Coordinator's value will be chosen under. An undefined unit that conflicts with the N governing runs per scenario is a substantive gap in the baseline method, not a style nit, so MAJOR stands.

The required fix is appropriate: define m per repetition slot, or as a per-scenario N + r, and state the outcome of a scenario that ends with fewer governing runs than required.

I checked this against BA-10 V3 at 1625a306, the V2 sheet, V2.1 1.3, 1.4, 1.6, 21.1, 21.3 and 21.7, AR2-43 (section 211.2), and the phase-2 findings BA10-02, BA10-03 and BA10-05. The defect is real and the item stands.

1. **The unit of the cap is not stated.** Line 65 defines PARAM-04 as a cap "m >= 1 on the attempts of a scenario", with "(2) every attempt counts toward m". In V2.1 21.3 an attempt is any entry in the per-scenario attempt log, and "every governing attempt counts". The same section separates scheduled repeats from retries. Line 40 now requires a scenario to run N governing times, and line 50 says N counts planned governing runs, not attempts. Nothing reconciles m with N. Read per scenario with every attempt counted, any m below N makes the scenario impossible to complete, yet the stated domain m >= 1 allows that. Read as a cap on retries (justification (1) frames m as bounding the review of INVALID retries), the per-slot unit is never written down.

2. **The partial-run case has no rule.** Rule (4) covers only a scenario that reaches m "without a governing run". A scenario that stops with 1 <= k < N governing runs gets no stated consequence. Rule (4) calls that group INVALID ("there is no governing run", V2.1 1.3), which does not fit this case either.

3. **Nothing else closes the gap.** AR2-43 fixes the method (a procedural cap, no host evidence, contamination counts) but no unit. I searched BA-04 V3, BA-07 V3, BA-11 V3 and V2.2 to V2.4: none of them defines MAX_ATTEMPTS relative to repetitions. The V2 method (m consecutive INVALID attempts at rate r) was implicitly per slot, and V3 withdrew it without stating a replacement unit.

4. **The gap came from the V3 fixes themselves.** It appeared when the BA10-02 fix (a per-scenario N) was combined with the BA10-05/AR2-43 fix ("every attempt counts").

**Why I lower the severity to MINOR.**
- The gap cannot produce a false PASS. Under V2.1 1.3 a group is PASS only if every required governing run passes, and 1.6 then gives NOT_EVALUATED. A missing required run can never become PASS or TRUE.
- m is still UNSET and the Coordinator records it knowing N. A bad value (for example m = 3 with N = 29) blocks the scenarios; it does not weaken the guarantee.
- The Architect rated BA10-05 MINOR, and it was the same kind of gap: what counts toward MAX_ATTEMPTS (the contamination question).

It still needs the requested fix, one or two sentences in BA-10 s2.2 PARAM-04. Either state m per planned governing-run slot, or write the per-scenario cap as N_s + r. Then state that a scenario ending with fewer than the required governing runs leaves its group non-PASS, under V2.1 1.3 and 1.6.

**What the finding required.** BA10-06 (MINOR; docs/automation/evidence/I-52-ct21d-phase2-architect-review.json) found two problems in the V2 PARAM-05 policy:
- The label was `MC-<SHA-256(MachineGuid)>`, yet "any attribute change = new class". Two different classes could therefore carry the same label.
- The build fields (AutoCAD build, `acad.exe` SHA-256) were placed in the class, although V2.1 2.1 classifies them as BUILD_BOUND.

The required fix offered two options joined by OR, plus one condition:
- Option 1: derive the label from a canonical hash over all class-defining attributes.
- Option 2: restrict the attributes to the MachineGuid plus the MACHINE_PROFILE_BOUND fields, and leave the BUILD_BOUND fields to the build tuple.
- Either way, keep the policy as a proposal for Owner or CAD-manager confirmation.

The governing decision is AR2-43 (decisions/I-52.md section 211.2). It requires PARAM-05 to be a proposed policy for Owner or CAD-manager confirmation, with a label value that needs a machine-attribute observation under a future host gate.

**What V3 does.** In BA-10 V3 section 2.2, lines 67-75, and summary row line 35, V3 applies both options, not just one:
- **Line 72:** the class-defining attributes are the MachineGuid plus the MACHINE_PROFILE_BOUND fields. The BUILD_BOUND fields (for example the `acad.exe` SHA-256) stay in the build tuple and are explicitly left out of the label.
- **Line 73:** the label is `MC-` plus the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the canonical serialization of all class-defining attributes. The serialization cites BA-07 V3 section 4, which exists and is titled "Canonical serialization and hash".
- **Line 74:** a change of any class-defining attribute makes a new class. The label and the class rule are now consistent.
- **Line 67:** the policy stays a conservative proposal for Owner or CAD-manager confirmation (Q-O5, line 122).
- **Line 75:** the label value needs a read-only observation under a future, unauthorized host gate. This matches AR2-43, and BA-11 V3 lines 67, 95 and 135 carry the same dependency.

**Why the reviewer's residual does not make the fix partial.**
- *Circularity.* The objection is that "the MACHINE_PROFILE_BOUND fields" include V2.1 line 237 ("machine identity class", which is the label itself). That same wording appears in the required fix's own option 2 ("MachineGuid plus MACHINE_PROFILE_BOUND fields"). V3 reproduced the prescribed fix word for word, so the objection is to the fix, not a gap in V3's closure.
- *Reading of the text.* V3 lists the attributes explicitly (OS version and build, profile, SECURELOAD, TRUSTEDPATHS) and adds the clear MachineGuid. MachineGuid is the concrete value behind the label row, so the label obviously cannot be an input to itself.
- *Option 1 alone is enough.* The label now hashes every class-defining attribute, so two different classes can no longer share a label. That was the actual inconsistency.
- *Module entries (EXEC-11).* The concern that including the manifest machine-layer module entries creates a sequencing dependency is not what BA10-06 asked about. It is already reported separately as BA10-V3-03 and should be judged on its own merits, at most MINOR.
